### 5.5 Rule-10 consequences (no proof reads another file's definition)

1. **Every new lemma is proved through published equations only.** Each one sits beside its
   definition or reads it through that definition's lemma:
   - `listToNat_eq`, `natToList_eq`/`natToList_length_listToNat`, `subStr_pairEncode`,
     `mulStr_pairEncode`, `leStr_pairEncode`, `primeStr_eq`, `rejectBlocksL_eq`, `statClose_iff`;
   - `uexp_def`, which replaces `Sampling`'s `unfold uexp` (the (b) row at `Sampling.lean` 207; the
     `PublicKeyLemmas` row at 845 goes with its deletion);
   - `pushesUniform_equiv`/`_fst`.

   Core definitions are read only through their lemmas (`Option.guard_apply`, not
   `simp [Option.guard]`; the latter is in rsa's stub and in `rabin_rbFind_eq`, which S2 deletes).
2. **A citation must not create a read.**
   - Re-pointing `dlc_castEquiv` to `finCastEquiv` would turn `dlc_splitEquiv_symm_ofFn`'s
     `subst h; exact ofFn_splitCoins_symm …` into a definitional read of `HardCoreLemmas`'
     definition. Mathlib's `Equiv.arrowCongr (finCongr h) (Equiv.refl Bool)` may reduce there,
     so G11 cites Mathlib.
   - In general, a deleted private definition that was read by `rfl`/`show` in its own file may be
     replaced only by a Mathlib/core term or a lemma, never by another file's definition.
3. **Statements only.**
   - dl-c reads `sampleBelowL` only through `sampleBelowL_eq_rejectBlocksL`.
   - rsa and rabin read their own samplers. rabin reads rsa's unit sampler only through
     `polyTimeComputable_unitSampleStr`.
   - No consumer unfolds `rejectBlocksL` (foreign to every consumer).
   - The host's existential hides its machine, so no consumer can read it.
4. **Matchers.** The host's proof splits the repetition host's `match` by `split` (the dl-a E1
   pattern). The seal includes `polyTimeComputable_iterateFind.match_1`.
5. **"Touched" is computed against the PR base.** It covers every changed file. S1 touches only the
   new lemmas, the deleted copies, the re-pointed fill declarations (which were seal-clean at
   landing) and `Sampling`'s `abs_uexp_sub_le` (fixed). It deliberately avoids `Closure`'s
   `ptc_comp` users (§5.4).

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/maintainer/tooling-followups.md =====

# Maintainer tooling follow-ups

## Gate 04 round 5, R5-01: anonymous commands

**Open.** The term collector's source tier enumerates stored constants and supplemental named
lemma statements. A standalone anonymous `example` can have no stored constant and be the sole
reader of a foreign definition. The auditor demonstrated this with `HiddenNat`; merely collecting
every stored constant does not close the gap.

Before relying on this collector alone for a future whole-file review:

- collect and check anonymous commands, or seal a conservative list of ordinary foreign TCSlib
  definitions from the module's import closure;
- retain the existing private/generated-helper traversal, approved notation handling and the
  explicit-unfold check;
- add a control whose only foreign-definition read is in an anonymous command: it closes unsealed
  and fails sealed.

The collector implementation is Lean. Any change to its `.lean` source goes through a PR under
the standing Lean-only-by-PR rule. Gate 04's head was independently covered by the auditor's
broader 6,322-pair import-closure seal; that result is not a repair of the collector.

The scanner's separate blank/comment-only continuation bug is **fixed** in the round-5 review:
12 text-parser regression cases pass, and the hardened scan of the audited head remains 0/0/0.
It remains a TCSlib-name text scanner, not a complete Lean syntax or core/Mathlib unfold check.

For gate 08 intake, account for this coverage qualification if the same stored-constant collector
is used; do not inherit an unqualified whole-command-coverage claim from its presence.

Source: [Gate 04 round 5 resolutions](../gates/04-s2b/resolutions-r5.md) and the verbatim findings.

## Gate 08 round 2: head-specific conservative coverage

At `84f35910912bd3d1cd520beea9469e0ed45ce504`, the supplement in
`gates/08-shared/evidence-r2/` checks 13,056 import-closure pairs: 12,966 active local seals
and 90 already irreducible pairs. It covers anonymous commands conservatively and includes
a standalone anonymous control under the full RSA seal. This does **not** close the general
collector implementation issue above. Numerical and hygienic private Names are resolved from
the environment; failed attribute/harness attempts are excluded before classification.

The 17 failing untouched declarations all have code identical to the checked base (comments
and following namespace commands excluded); broad base seals were not rerun. Fifteen match

`NumberTheory/Primality.exists_samplePrime_nuppt`. See `conservative-failure-preservation.json`

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/fills/fill-environment-addendum.md =====

# Fill-agent environment addendum (Pass–shelat ch. 5–8 campaign, v1): resources, the dependency cache, starting Lean

**Version 1 (2026-11-06).** Attached to every fill brief of this campaign (branch
`cryptography/pass-shelat-ch2-4` and its descendants). Part 1 is the Arora–Barak campaign's
addendum v2.6, Part 1, unchanged: it is generic to TCSlib at this Lean pin (4.25.0). That
addendum's Part 2 (a `readlink` shim) and Part 3 (megafills) are **not** authorized here:
- if Lean fails to start with `error: failed to locate application`, stop with escalation E-RES
  and report the error; do not work around it;
- one session works on one brief.

Fills of this campaign may run in parallel on separate hosts (user, 2026-11-06). On one host,
**one Lean process at a time** (a module check, a probe, a bootstrap or sweep step, each through
`scripts/lean_check_tree.sh`, or one `lake exe cache get`); the cache tool's own internal jobs are
not counted. Everything in your brief stays binding.

## Part 1: resources and the dependency cache

**Why.** Four fill workers of 2026-10-17 stopped before any proof check, all for host reasons. The
dependency cache filled the disk (`No space left on device`, `leantar` exit 101). One worker staged
files on `/dev/shm`, which counts against the memory limit, and others copied dependency trees
between directories. Empty or truncated oleans, a stale compiled Lake configuration and a Lake
re-clone of Mathlib (package URLs differing from the manifest) followed. Lean then crashed
(SIGBUS 135, SIGSEGV 139) or stalled at a full memory limit. The rules below stop that early and
cleanly.

1. **Preflight, before any cache or Lean work.** Record in `evidence/logs/preflight.log`, and quote
   in `REPORT.md`:
   - `nproc`;
   - the memory limit and use: the cgroup's `memory.max`, `memory.current`, `memory.events` and
     `memory.stat` (cgroup v1: `memory.limit_in_bytes`, `memory.usage_in_bytes`, `memory.stat`),
     or `/proc/meminfo` where there is no cgroup limit;
   - `df -B1` and the filesystem type (`df -T`) of the clone's directory and of every scratch
     directory you use.

   **Stop with escalation E-RES**, quoting the numbers, if the clone's filesystem has less than
   **12 GiB free**, or the memory headroom is below **4 GiB**. Do not try to make room by copying,
   moving or deduplicating dependency trees.
   - **When the disk floor applies.** The 12 GiB floor applies at this initial preflight, which
     covers everything after it, the toolchain included. If you install the toolchain after it,
     you may re-check before `lake exe cache get`; that re-check's floor is **8 GiB** (the
     packages about 6 GiB, the cache archives about 1 GiB, the bootstrap's oleans and the clone).
     After the cache step, disk is not re-checked: an ENOSPC is handled by item 4.
   - **The memory headroom is the limit minus the memory in use**, where the memory in use is
     `anon + kernel + shmem` from `memory.stat` (cgroup v1: `memory.usage_in_bytes − total_cache +
     total_shmem`). Where `memory.max` is `max` (no cgroup limit), the headroom is `MemAvailable`
     from `/proc/meminfo`. Log the fields and the computation.
   - **Not shortages:** page cache (`file`, `active_file`, `inactive_file`, `file_mapped` in
     `memory.stat`; `memory.current` includes it), and `memory.events`' `max` and `high` counters,
     which count reclaim at the limit. The kernel reclaims the cache as Lean needs memory.
   - **A shortage** is an `oom` or `oom_kill` event, a Lean exit 137, or a headroom below 4 GiB
     as computed here.
   - **Measured needs at this pin:** the Mathlib cache is about 5.2 GiB unpacked (all packages, with
     their git checkouts, about 6 GiB), plus about 1 GiB of archives kept by the cache tool; the
     toolchain about 4.2 GiB with its archive. The TCSlib bootstrap writes about 0.2–0.3 GB of
     oleans. Lean's peak memory is about 2.8 GiB (`Build/Catalog`, at `-j4`; 2,796 MiB measured on a
     fill host); most modules need under 1.6 GB.
2. **One checkout, one cache.** Do everything in a single clone.
   - **Fetch the cache for your brief's Mathlib roots only**, into that clone's own
     `.lake/packages`, with `TAR_OPTIONS=--no-same-owner` in its environment (extract the
     toolchain archive the same way if it fails on ownership). The roots are the Mathlib modules
     that the modules of your brief's order list import directly; from the clone's root, after
     your brief's first edit (its imports or overlay, if any):

     ```sh
     ORDER=<your brief's order list>
     sed 's|$|.lean|' "$ORDER" | xargs grep -h '^import Mathlib' | awk '{print $2}' | sort -u \
       > evidence/logs/mathlib-roots.txt
     TAR_OPTIONS=--no-same-owner lake exe cache get $(cat evidence/logs/mathlib-roots.txt) \
       2>&1 | tee evidence/logs/cache-get.log
     ```

     The tool fetches those modules and everything they import. **Never run the unfiltered
     `lake exe cache get`.** Record the roots' count and the number of files fetched. If you add
     an import later (only where your brief authorizes one), fetch for the new roots the same way.
     Alternatively, symlink `.lake/packages` to a populated tree at exactly the same pins,
     recorded in `REPORT.md`.
   - **Log the cache tool's archive store first** (v2.5). Before the first `lake exe cache get`,
     record in `evidence/logs/cache-store.log` whether the store exists
     (`${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/mathlib` by default), how many files it holds and their
     total size (`find … -type f | wc -l`, `du -sb …`). The fetch log's "Attempting to download N"
     and "Decompressing M" then show that `M − N` archives were already in the store. Archives
     already there are the cache tool's own, named by hash and checked by it: using them is
     allowed, and the store is not "another session's object store" (below). In `REPORT.md`, give
     their number and, if you know it, their origin (an earlier session on this host, the host
     image); do not describe them as downloaded by this session.
   - Never copy, move, merge or deduplicate dependency trees between directories.
   - Never reuse another session's scratch tree, package builds, toolchain or object store, and
     never join `LEAN_PATH`s across trees.
   - Never put the clone, `.lake`, the cache, an olean tree (`TCSLIB_OLEANS`) or `TMPDIR` on a
     memory-backed filesystem (`/dev/shm`, any tmpfs).
   - **The cache tool's own work is outside the one-Lean rule.** `lake exe cache get` may first
     compile the cache executable (on a fresh clone, about 20 Lake jobs, among them a few
     Batteries modules) and runs `lake build --no-build proofwidgets:release`. Lake schedules
     these jobs itself, and at this pin it has no option to serialize them. They are expected and
     allowed. They are not a `lake build` of the project, and they are not "a Lean process" in the
     sense of Part 3, item 5. Run the command alone: start no check of your own until it has
     exited. Do not reconstruct, measure or certify Lake's internal scheduling, and do not report
     it as a deviation.
   - **Packages match the manifest** (v2.5: the packages present). A fresh clone's first
     `lake exe cache get …` fetches the packages that `lake-manifest.json` names, except those the
     narrowed fetch does not need. Afterwards, and before every later Lake command, check each
     package **present in** `.lake/packages`: `git -C .lake/packages/<name> remote get-url origin`
     and `rev-parse HEAD` must equal the manifest's URL and revision. If one differs, stop with
     E-RES. List the manifest's packages that were not cloned as **ABSENT**, not as a mismatch (at
     this pin `doc-gen4`, `UnicodeBasic`, `BibtexQuery` and `MD4Lean`, the documentation
     toolchain). The check passes when every present package matches and no module of your order
     list imports an absent package; quote its last line in `REPORT.md`. Never let Lake re-clone
     or update a package that is already present.
3. **Check the cache before the bootstrap.**
   - The narrowed `lake exe cache get` exited 0, with no failed download.
   - `find .lake/packages -name '*.olean' -size 0` prints nothing.
   - A probe that imports one of your roots elaborates through `scripts/lean_check_tree.sh`, e.g.
     a file containing only the first line of `mathlib-roots.txt` as an `import`. A probe that
     imports no Mathlib does not test the cache, and a module outside your roots' closure is not
     in your cache.
   - **Failed downloads** (a network error such as a proxy `403`, or `N download(s) failed`):
     re-run the same narrowed command up to twice; it fetches only what is missing. If files
     still fail, that is a failed check of this item (item 4).
4. **One cleaned retry, then stop.** Clean and retry once on any of these:
   - ENOSPC (`No space left on device`, `os error 28`);
   - `leantar` exit 101;
   - Lean exit 135 (SIGBUS), 137 (killed) or 139 (SIGSEGV);
   - `compiled configuration is invalid`;
   - a failed check of item 3.

   To clean, delete the clone's `.lake/packages` and its compiled configurations
   (`.lake/lakefile.olean*`), re-run the preflight (a re-check: item 1's floor before the cache),
   and run the narrowed `lake exe cache get` once more. If anything fails again, stop with E-RES
   and report, naming the files that failed to download and the roots you fetched. **Never**
   unpack or restore individual archives or oleans by hand (`leantar`, the cache tool's `lookup`,
   copies from elsewhere).
5. **Bootstrap order.** Your brief's order list is the bootstrap. You may build, first, only the
   modules of the list that your owned file imports (directly or not), in the list's order, and
   check your owned file against them. Build the list's remaining modules before the final
   sweep. Record which you did.
6. **No self-imposed timeouts.** Do not wrap module checks in short timeouts.
   - Log each module's start and end time, and its maximum memory (`/usr/bin/time -v` where
     available).
   - A module that stalls far beyond the measured figures is a resource symptom: re-read the
     memory counters, and compute the headroom as in item 1 (the memory in use, not
     `memory.current`). Stop with E-RES only on a shortage as item 1 defines it.
7. **Logs in place.** Write every log to its final path under `evidence/logs/` from the start
   (`2>&1 | tee …`). Never move a log that a running process is writing.
8. **No checks against missing prerequisites.** If the bootstrap stops, record its tail and skip
   the checks that need its products. Do not report their failures as findings.

E-RES is an environment report, not a failed fill. A continuation goes to a host that passes the
preflight.

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared/evidence-r2/H15-registry-extract.md =====

# H15 registry excerpt

Source: `machine-library-design.md`, on the records branch. SHA-256 of the full source
file at this preparation: `79574cc5abbf4de0341f1401960a781efd4368ab96f34303e538bd2d4e317adb`. The final dispatch pins
the records commit. This excerpt copies the rule and the exact H14/H15 rows; intervening rows
are omitted. Verify H15 in the full source, not only this excerpt.

## 14. Hosts first: the rule and the host registry (user, 2026-10-12)

**The rule** (`policy.md` §1, **Hosts come first**; `workflow.md` §2 and §4,
ground rule 4). A *host* is a control structure that drives other routines:
a search or traversal, a recursion or evaluation scheme, an interpreter step
block, a clocked or windowed runner, a dispatcher over a data structure, or an
input device. A host is never built `private` inside the proof that first
needs it. Its public contract is designed and statement-gated first, generic
in what its consumers vary, with time and head-envelope clauses; consumers
cite it, proved modulo while its fill runs. Leaf rows (copy, compare, seek,
arithmetic) are not hosts and keep the §4 rule of admission.

| # | Host | Status | Named consumers |
|---|---|---|---|
| H14 | **Clean-module host** (`TuringMachine/Build/ModuleHost.lean`, namespace `Turing.ModuleHost`): the first-halting clean-module contract `Clean` (a module with a work tape halts first, at a positive time within a budget of its argument's length, at the seam holding a result word, having emitted a declared chunk), the clean install and emit modules of every polynomial-time word function (`clean_install`, `clean_emit`), and the finite host `hostTM` running `n` such modules over a shared bank of work tapes, generic in the modules, the control states and their table, the return map and the start state (`host_call`, `host_clean`, `guard_add`, `hostTM_step_inl`); head envelopes `Clean.envelope` (a clean module's heads stay within `B \|arg\|` cells of the origin at every time), `host_call_envelope` (within `t` cells up to time `t` of a call) and `host_clean_envelope` (`host_clean` with the envelope `B \|arg\|` throughout the call), the coarse envelopes from the time bounds and the unit head moves of `Turing.MultiTapeTM.workTapePos_step_le` | **public; harvested 2026-11-05 (gate 03l, R-03l-1); contract gated at gate 03l's delta round; head-envelope clauses added 2026-11-06 (gate 03l round 2, finding 1).** Harvested from the private module layer of `ClassNP/SAT.lean` (on `main`) and its copy in `Randomized/Build/IterateFindHost.lean` (duplication ledger DL-16); both copies are deleted. The copier `copyTM` of `IterateFindHost` re-derives the private input copier of `TuringMachine/Build/EmitIterBody.lean` (16 % line overlap, gate 03l review §6.1 (d)): a parallel routine, not a copy | `ClassNP/SAT.lean` (the streaming emitter behind `SAT_reducible_SAT3`: six modules, one control state); `Randomized/Build/IterateFind.lean`, through `Randomized/Build/IterateFindHost.lean` (the repetition machine behind `polyTimeComputable_iterateFind`: five modules, three control states) |
| H15 | **Block-rejection string-function host:** `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.polyTimeComputable_rejectBlocksL`, in `TCSlib/Cryptography/Candidates/Concrete.lean`. Given a parameter-dependent decidable test `E`, a polynomial-time bit test on paired parameter/value words, and polynomial-time words `par`, `kw`, `bw`, `tw`, `c`, publishes an existential polynomial-time output `g`: rejection is `g z = []`; otherwise the value is read from `(g z).tail`, whose length is at most `(kw z).length`. Sizes and trial count are the supplied words' lengths; no `k ≤ B`, positivity or full-coin-length premise is imposed. Depends on `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind` (the repetition host in `Randomized/Repetition.lean`, via `Build/IterateFind.lean` and the H14 clean-module host). This layer exposes polynomial time and the payload-length bound; a separate machine head-envelope clause is not exposed. | **Statement only**, in PR #227; gate 08 pending (round-1 finding G08-01 repaired by this registry entry). The host proof is `sorry`, assigned to the **external S2 fill** under Q4 (B); it is not proved or dispatched by this registration. The user dispatches S2 after gate closure and #227's merge. Registered 2026-11-06 PST. | **dl-a:** `polyTimeComputable_expSampleRaw`; **dl-c:** `dlc_numPoly_sample`, serving ElGamal generators/encryption; **rsa:** the unit sampler and `rsaGenRaw`; **rabin:** the prime/Blum-prime generators, with the tail bound feeding padding. S2 replaces their four private rejection loops and refreshes the six sketches (Q7). |

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared/evidence-r2/bootstrap.py =====

"""Sequential native macOS bootstrap; run from the campaign root with python3 -I."""

from pathlib import Path
import datetime
import hashlib
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time


record_root = Path.cwd()
root = Path("/Users/seyoonr/.codex/worktrees/ps-gate08-repair/tcslib-pass-shelat-ch2-4")
out = record_root / "briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared/evidence-r2"
logs = out / "logs"
logs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
modules = (out / "order.txt").read_text().splitlines()
base = (out / "HEAD.txt").read_text().strip()
env = os.environ.copy()
env["TCSLIB_OLEANS"] = str(record_root / ".lake/ps-maintainer/oleans-gate08-r2")


def now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()


fingerprints = []
for module in modules:
    path = module + ".lean"
    expected = subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", base + ":" + path])
    actual = (root / path).read_bytes()
    assert actual == expected, "source differs from pinned base: " + path
    fingerprints.append(hashlib.sha256(actual).hexdigest() + "  " + path)
(out / "source-sha256.txt").write_text("\n".join(fingerprints) + "\n")

with (logs / "bootstrap.log").open("w") as summary:
    def record(line):
        summary.write(line + "\n")
        summary.flush()
        print(line, flush=True)

    record("START " + now() + " BASE " + base)
    record("TCSLIB_OLEANS " + env["TCSLIB_OLEANS"])
    for index, module in enumerate(modules, 1):
        log = logs / "modules" / (module + ".log")
        log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        start = now()
        elapsed = time.monotonic()
        with log.open("w") as handle:
            handle.write("START " + start + "\n")
            handle.flush()
            process = subprocess.Popen(
                ["/usr/bin/time", "-l", "bash", "scripts/lean_check_tree.sh", module],
                stdout=handle,
                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                env=env,
                cwd=root,
            )
            (logs / "bootstrap.pid").write_text(str(process.pid) + "\n")
            rc = process.wait()
            end = now()
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - elapsed
            handle.write("\nEND " + end + " RC " + str(rc) + "\n")
        text = log.read_text()
        rss = re.search(r"(\d+)\s+maximum resident set size", text)
        record(
            f"{index}/{len(modules)} {module} rc={rc} "
            f"elapsed={elapsed:.3f}s rss_bytes={rss.group(1) if rss else 'unavailable'} "
            f"start={start} end={end}"
        )
        if rc:
            record("STOP at " + module + "; prerequisites for later checks are unavailable")
            sys.exit(rc)
    record("DONE " + now())

"""Expanded collector, whole-file seals and controls after bootstrap; python3 -I at record root."""
from pathlib import Path
import datetime
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

root = Path.cwd()
wt = Path("/Users/seyoonr/.codex/worktrees/ps-gate08-repair/tcslib-pass-shelat-ch2-4")
gate = root / "briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared"
out = gate / "evidence-r2"
logs = out / "logs"
scratch = root / ".lake/ps-maintainer/gate08-r2"
env = os.environ.copy()
copied = json.loads((out / "copied-tree.json").read_text())
assert copied["rebuilt_verified"]
assert copied["head"] == (out / "HEAD.txt").read_text().strip()
required = {path[:-5] for path in (out / "source-targets.txt").read_text().splitlines()}
assert required <= {row["module"] for row in copied["modules"]}
env["TCSLIB_OLEANS"] = copied["target"]
assert subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(wt), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip() == \
    (out / "HEAD.txt").read_text().strip()


def check(module, name):
    log = logs / name
    # Resume only completed checks in this pinned run, with their exact saved probe source.
    if log.exists():
        stem = module.rsplit("/", 1)[1]
        saved = out / "seal" / (stem + ".source.txt") if name.startswith("sealed-") else out / (stem + ".source.txt")
        text = log.read_text()
        ended = re.search(r"(?m)^END .+ RC (-?\d+)$", text)
        if ended and saved.exists():
            assert (root / (module + ".lean")).read_bytes() == saved.read_bytes()
            rc = int(ended.group(1))
            print(module + f" rc={rc} (completed pinned check retained)", flush=True)
            return rc, text
    with log.open("w") as handle:
        handle.write("START " + datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat() + "\n")
        handle.flush()
        p = subprocess.Popen(
            ["/usr/bin/time", "-l", "bash", "scripts/lean_check_tree.sh", module],
            stdout=handle, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, env=env, cwd=root)
        (logs / "checks.pid").write_text(str(p.pid) + "\n")
        rc = p.wait()
        handle.write("\nEND " + datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat() + f" RC {rc}\n")
    print(module + f" rc={rc}", flush=True)
    return rc, log.read_text()


prefix = ".lake/ps-maintainer/gate08-r2/"
rc, collected = check(prefix + "CollectExpanded", "collect-expanded.log")
assert rc == 0
assert "TOUCHED-NOT-FOUND" not in collected and "AXIOMS-NOT-FOUND" not in collected
names = {}
for module, name in re.findall(r"SEALROW (\S+) \| (\S+) \|", collected):
    if name not in {"Complexity.PolyExpr.eval", "TCSlib.Cryptography.glNeed"}:
        names.setdefault(module, set()).add(name)
targets = (out / "source-targets.txt").read_text().splitlines()
modules = {path[:-5].replace("/", "."): path for path in targets}
for module in modules:
    names.setdefault(module, set())
assert set(names) == set(modules)
union = set().union(*names.values())
(out / "seal").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
additions = []
for module, path in modules.items():
    stem = Path(path).stem
    old = {line.strip() for line in (gate / "evidence/seal" / f"names-{stem}.txt").read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()}
    assert old <= names[module], (module, old - names[module])
    additions.extend((module, name) for name in sorted(names[module] - old))
    (out / "seal" / f"names-{stem}.txt").write_text("\n".join(sorted(names[module])) + "\n")
(out / "seal/names-ALL.txt").write_text("\n".join(sorted(union)) + "\n")
axioms = re.findall(r"AXIOMS (\S+) \| (\S+) \| \[([^\]]*)\]", collected)
assert len(axioms) == 146, len(axioms)
for _, name, printed in axioms:
    actual = {part.strip() for part in printed.split(",") if part.strip()}
    permitted = {"propext", "Classical.choice", "Quot.sound"}
    if name.endswith(".polyTimeComputable_rejectBlocksL"):
        permitted.add("sorryAx")
    assert actual <= permitted, (name, actual)

sorry_names = [name for _, name, axioms_ in axioms if "sorryAx" in axioms_]
assert sorry_names == ["TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.polyTimeComputable_rejectBlocksL"], sorry_names
(out / "axioms-touched.tsv").write_text("\n".join("\t".join(row) for row in axioms) + "\n")

expected = {
    "Concrete": {"primesPairEquiv_apply_val"},
    "DiscreteLog": {"ExpGroupGen.FullLength.exists_fullLengthExcept"},
    "Rabin": {"rabinCollection_index", "rabinBlumTrapdoor_index"},
    "Basic": {"uexp_mono"},
    "Factoring": {"exists_plantFactorer"},
}
seal_results = []
for module, path in modules.items():
    stem = Path(path).stem
    probe = scratch / f"Sealed{stem}.lean"
    nf = out / "seal" / f"names-{stem}.txt"
    subprocess.run(["python3", "-I", str(gate / "evidence/tools/mkseal.py"),
                    str(wt / path), str(probe), str(nf)], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
    (out / "seal" / f"Sealed{stem}.source.txt").write_bytes(probe.read_bytes())
    rc, text = check(prefix + "Sealed" + stem, f"sealed-{stem}.log")
    details = subprocess.check_output([
        "python3", "-I", str(gate / "evidence/tools/errdecl.py"), str(probe),
        str(logs / f"sealed-{stem}.log"),
        str(gate / "evidence/seal" / f"touched-{stem}.txt")], text=True)
    failures = set(re.findall(r"decl `([^`]+)`", details))
    assert failures == expected.get(stem, set()), (stem, failures, details)
    assert "touched=True" not in details, details
    assert (rc == 0) == (not failures), (stem, rc, failures)
    (out / "seal" / f"Sealed{stem}.errors.txt").write_text(details)
    seal_results.append({"module": module, "rc": rc, "untouched_failures": sorted(failures)})

imports = "\n".join(line for line in (out / "CollectExpanded.source.txt").read_text().splitlines()
                    if line.startswith("import "))
body = (gate / "evidence/tools/controls_body.lean").read_text()
extra = """
namespace S1PrimeControl
example (w : List Bool) : primeStr w = [decide (listToNat w).Prime] := rfl
end S1PrimeControl
"""
plain = imports + "\n" + body + extra
sealed = imports + "\nattribute [local irreducible] " + " ".join(sorted(union)) + "\n" + body + extra
for name, source in [("ControlsUnsealed", plain), ("ControlsSealed", sealed)]:
    (scratch / (name + ".lean")).write_text(source)
    (out / (name + ".source.txt")).write_text(source)
    rc, text = check(prefix + name, name + ".log")
    errors = len(re.findall(r"\.lean:\d+:\d+: error:", text))
    assert (rc == 0 and errors == 0) if name.endswith("Unsealed") else (rc != 0 and errors == 14), \
        (name, rc, errors)

result = {
    "head": (out / "HEAD.txt").read_text().strip(),
    "unique_names": len(union), "added_pairs": additions,
    "touched_axiom_prints": len(axioms), "touched_sorry_names": sorry_names,
    "seal_results": seal_results, "touched_failures": 0,
    "controls_unsealed_passed": 14, "controls_sealed_failed": 14,
    "original_base_controls_rerun": False,
}
(out / "expanded-checks-summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
print(json.dumps({key: value for key, value in result.items() if key != "seal_results"}), flush=True)

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared/evidence-r2/conservative-checks.py =====

"""Import-closure supplemental seals; run as python3 -I from the records root."""
from pathlib import Path
import datetime
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess

root = Path.cwd()
gate = root / "briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared"
out = gate / "evidence-r2"
wt = Path("/Users/seyoonr/.codex/worktrees/ps-gate08-repair/tcslib-pass-shelat-ch2-4")
head = (out / "HEAD.txt").read_text().strip()
assert subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(wt), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip() == head
copied = json.loads((out / "copied-tree.json").read_text())
assert copied["rebuilt_verified"] and copied["head"] == head
env = os.environ.copy()
env["TCSLIB_OLEANS"] = copied["target"]
scratch = root / ".lake/ps-maintainer/gate08-r2"
data = out / "conservative"
data.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


def check(stem, source):
    probe = scratch / (stem + ".lean")
    saved = data / (stem + ".source.txt")
    log = out / "logs" / (stem + ".log")
    if log.exists() and saved.exists():
        previous = log.read_text()
        ended = re.search(r"(?m)^END .+ RC (-?\d+)$", previous)
        if ended:
            assert saved.read_text() == source and probe.read_text() == source
            rc = int(ended.group(1))
            print(stem + f" rc={rc} (completed pinned check retained)", flush=True)
            return rc, previous
    probe.write_text(source)
    saved.write_text(source)
    with log.open("w") as handle:
        handle.write("START " + datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat() + "\n")
        handle.flush()
        rc = subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/time", "-l", "bash", "scripts/lean_check_tree.sh",
                             str(probe.relative_to(root))[:-5]], cwd=root, env=env,
                            stdout=handle, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT).returncode
        handle.write("\nEND " + datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat() + f" RC {rc}\n")
    print(stem + f" rc={rc}", flush=True)
    return rc, log.read_text()


def imports(module):
    source = (wt / (module.replace(".", "/") + ".lean")).read_text()
    return [m for m in re.findall(r"(?m)^import\s+(\S+)", source) if m.startswith("TCSlib.")]


def closure(module):
    found = set()
    stack = imports(module)
    while stack:
        item = stack.pop()
        if item not in found:
            found.add(item)
            stack.extend(imports(item))
    return sorted(found)


targets = (out / "source-targets.txt").read_text().splitlines()
modules = {path[:-5].replace("/", "."): path for path in targets}
closures = {module: closure(module) for module in modules}
(data / "import-closures.json").write_text(json.dumps(closures, indent=2) + "\n")
imports_source = "\n".join(line for line in (out / "CollectExpanded.source.txt").read_text().splitlines()
                           if line.startswith("import "))
collector = r'''
open Lean Meta Elab Command
syntax (name := closureSealCmd) "#sealclosure " ident "[" ident,* "]" : command
@[command_elab closureSealCmd] def closureSeal : CommandElab := fun stx => do
  let audited := stx[1].getId
  let deps := stx[3].getSepArgs.map Syntax.getId
  let env ← getEnv
  for dep in deps do
    unless (env.getModuleIdx? dep).isSome do throwError "missing dependency {dep}"
  let mut rows : Array String := #[]
  for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
    let some mi := env.getModuleIdxFor? n | continue
    let home := env.header.moduleNames[mi.toNat]!
    unless deps.contains home do continue
    unless ci.isDefinition do continue
    if isInstanceCore env n then continue
    let matcher := (Match.Extension.getMatcherInfo? env n).isSome
    let status ← liftCoreM <| getReducibilityStatus n
    if !matcher && status == .reducible then continue
    if n == `Complexity.PolyExpr.eval || n == `TCSlib.Cryptography.glNeed then continue
    rows := rows.push s!"CLOSUREROW {audited} | {n} | {home}"
  for row in rows.qsort (· < ·) do logInfo m!"{row}"
'''
commands = "\n".join("#sealclosure " + module + " [" + ", ".join(deps) + "]"
                     for module, deps in closures.items())
rc, collected = check("CollectConservative", imports_source + "\n" + collector + commands + "\n")
assert rc == 0
names = {module: set() for module in modules}
for module, name in re.findall(r"CLOSUREROW (\S+) \| (\S+) \|", collected):
    names[module].add(name)

results = []
for module, path in modules.items():
    stem = Path(path).stem
    nf = data / ("names-" + stem + ".txt")
    nf.write_text("\n".join(sorted(names[module])) + "\n")
    small = {line for line in (out / "seal" / ("names-" + stem + ".txt")).read_text().splitlines() if line}
    assert small <= names[module], (module, small - names[module])
    probe = scratch / ("ClosureVerified" + stem + ".lean")
    source_lines = (wt / path).read_text().split("\n")
    i = next(k for k, line in enumerate(source_lines) if line.startswith("namespace "))
    j = i + 1
    while j < len(source_lines) and not source_lines[j].strip():
        j += 1
    insert = j if source_lines[j].startswith("open ") else i
    # Resolve printed names against the environment, including numerical/hygienic components.
    spellings = json.dumps(sorted(names[module]), ensure_ascii=False)
    seal = '''-- Import-closure seal, independent of stored-constant reads.
run_cmd do
  let env ← Lean.getEnv
  let mut catalog : Std.HashMap String (Array Lean.Name) := {}
  let mut active : Nat := 0
  let mut already : Nat := 0
  for (n, _) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
    let some mi := env.getModuleIdxFor? n | continue
    unless (`TCSlib).isPrefixOf env.header.moduleNames[mi.toNat]! do continue
    let ns := (catalog[n.toString]?).getD #[]
    catalog := catalog.insert n.toString (ns.push n)
  for spelling in (#''' + spellings + ''' : Array String) do
    let ns := (catalog[spelling]?).getD #[]
    unless ns.size == 1 do throwError "seal name not found or ambiguous: {spelling}"
    let n := ns[0]!
    let before ← Lean.Elab.Command.liftCoreM <| Lean.getReducibilityStatus n
    if before == .irreducible then
      already := already + 1
    else
      let id := Lean.mkIdent n
      Lean.Elab.Command.elabCommand (← `(command| attribute [local irreducible] $id:ident))
      active := active + 1
    let status ← Lean.Elab.Command.liftCoreM <| Lean.getReducibilityStatus n
    unless status == .irreducible do throwError "seal not installed: {n}"
  Lean.logInfo m!"SUPPLEMENT-SEAL active={active} already={already}"
-- END IMPORT-CLOSURE SEAL
'''
    source_lines.insert(insert + 1, seal)
    source = "\n".join(source_lines)
    rc, text = check("ClosureVerified" + stem, source)
    assert not re.search(r"unknownIdentifier|unexpected token|seal name not found|seal not installed", text), text
    seal_end = source.splitlines().index("-- END IMPORT-CLOSURE SEAL") + 1
    error_lines = [int(n) for n in re.findall(r"\.lean:(\d+):\d+: error", text)]
    assert all(n > seal_end for n in error_lines), (module, error_lines, seal_end)
    counts = re.findall(r"SUPPLEMENT-SEAL active=(\d+) already=(\d+)", text)
    assert len(counts) == 1 and sum(map(int, counts[0])) == len(names[module])
    details = subprocess.check_output(["python3", "-I", str(gate / "evidence/tools/errdecl.py"),
                                      str(probe), str(out / "logs" / ("ClosureVerified" + stem + ".log")),
                                      str(gate / "evidence/seal" / ("touched-" + stem + ".txt"))], text=True)
    (data / (stem + ".errors.txt")).write_text(details)
    results.append({"module": module, "candidate_count": len(names[module]),
                    "active_seals": int(counts[0][0]), "already_irreducible": int(counts[0][1]), "rc": rc,
                    "diagnostics": len(error_lines),
                    "declarations": re.findall(r"decl `([^`]*)`", details),
                    "touched_failure": "touched=True" in details})

# The sole foreign-definition read in this probe is in an anonymous example.
plain = "import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.Concrete\n" + \
        "example (w : List Bool) : TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.primeStr w = " + \
        "[decide (TCSlib.Cryptography.NumberTheory.listToNat w).Prime] := rfl\n"
sealed = plain.replace("example (w", "attribute [local irreducible] TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.primeStr\nexample (w")
rc_plain, _ = check("AnonymousFinalUnsealed", plain)
rc_sealed, text = check("AnonymousFinalSealed", sealed)
assert rc_plain == 0 and rc_sealed != 0 and len(re.findall(r"\.lean:\d+:\d+: error:", text)) == 1
assert "TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.primeStr" in names["TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.RSA"]
# Repeat the anonymous-only control with the actual complete RSA import-closure seal.
rsa_lines = (data / "ClosureVerifiedRSA.source.txt").read_text().splitlines()
start = rsa_lines.index("-- Import-closure seal, independent of stored-constant reads.")
end = rsa_lines.index("-- END IMPORT-CLOSURE SEAL") + 1
broad_seal = "\n".join(rsa_lines[start:end]) + "\n"
broad_plain = plain.replace("import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.Concrete", "import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.RSA")
import_line, example = broad_plain.split("\n", 1)
rc_broad_plain, _ = check("AnonymousBroadUnsealed", broad_plain)
rc_broad_sealed, broad_text = check("AnonymousBroadSealed", import_line + "\n" + broad_seal + example)
assert rc_broad_plain == 0 and rc_broad_sealed != 0
assert len(re.findall(r"\.lean:\d+:\d+: error:", broad_text)) == 1
summary = {"head": head, "probe_prefix": "ClosureVerified", "candidate_pairs": sum(map(len, names.values())), "seal_results": results,
           "touched_failures": sum(r["touched_failure"] for r in results),
           "anonymous_only_unsealed_rc": rc_plain, "anonymous_only_sealed_rc": rc_sealed,
           "anonymous_broad_unsealed_rc": rc_broad_plain, "anonymous_broad_sealed_rc": rc_broad_sealed,
           "exclusions": ["instances", "reducible nonmatchers", "Complexity.PolyExpr.eval", "TCSlib.Cryptography.glNeed"]}
(out / "conservative-summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + "\n")
print(json.dumps(summary), flush=True)

import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.Rabin
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.DiscreteLogHardcore
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.ElGamal
import TCSlib.Cryptography.ZeroKnowledge.ThreeColoring.ColZKLemmas
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PublicKeyLemmas

open Lean Meta Elab Command
syntax (name := closureSealCmd) "#sealclosure " ident "[" ident,* "]" : command
@[command_elab closureSealCmd] def closureSeal : CommandElab := fun stx => do
  let audited := stx[1].getId
  let deps := stx[3].getSepArgs.map Syntax.getId
  let env ← getEnv
  for dep in deps do
    unless (env.getModuleIdx? dep).isSome do throwError "missing dependency {dep}"
  let mut rows : Array String := #[]
  for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
    let some mi := env.getModuleIdxFor? n | continue
    let home := env.header.moduleNames[mi.toNat]!
    unless deps.contains home do continue
    unless ci.isDefinition do continue
    if isInstanceCore env n then continue
    let matcher := (Match.Extension.getMatcherInfo? env n).isSome
    let status ← liftCoreM <| getReducibilityStatus n
    if !matcher && status == .reducible then continue
    if n == `Complexity.PolyExpr.eval || n == `TCSlib.Cryptography.glNeed then continue
    rows := rows.push s!"CLOSUREROW {audited} | {n} | {home}"
  for row in rows.qsort (· < ·) do logInfo m!"{row}"

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared/evidence-r2/CollectExpanded.source.txt =====

import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.Rabin
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.DiscreteLogHardcore
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.ElGamal
import TCSlib.Cryptography.ZeroKnowledge.ThreeColoring.ColZKLemmas
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PublicKeyLemmas
open Lean Meta Elab Command

/-- user-facing name of a constant (private prefix removed) -/
def userStr (n : Name) : String := ((privateToUserName? n).getD n).toString

def matchesTouched (ts : List String) (n : Name) : Bool :=
  let s := userStr n
  ts.any fun t => s == t || s.endsWith ("." ++ t) ||
    (s.splitOn (t ++ ".")).length > 1 && (s.startsWith (t ++ ".") || (s.splitOn ("." ++ t ++ ".")).length > 1)

def isTCS (env : Environment) (c : Name) : Option Name :=
  match env.getModuleIdxFor? c with
  | some mi => let m := env.header.moduleNames[mi.toNat]!; if (`TCSlib).isPrefixOf m then some m else none
  | none => none

syntax (name := collectCmd) "#collect " ident "[" str,* "]" : command

@[command_elab collectCmd] def elabCollect : CommandElab := fun stx => do
  let modN := stx[1].getId
  let ts : List String := (stx[3].getSepArgs.map fun s => s.isStrLit?.getD "").toList
  let env ← getEnv
  let some modIdx := env.getModuleIdx? modN | throwError "no module {modN}"
  let mut ours : Array Name := #[]
  for (n, _) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
    if env.getModuleIdxFor? n == some modIdx && matchesTouched ts n then ours := ours.push n
  -- every touched name must be found
  for t in ts do
    unless ours.any (fun n => userStr n == t || (userStr n).endsWith ("." ++ t)) do
      logWarning m!"TOUCHED-NOT-FOUND {t}"
  -- wide pass: types of all constants reached; values of own-module definitions, transitively
  let mut cs : NameSet := {}
  let mut seen : NameSet := {}
  let mut stack : List Name := []
  for n in ours do
    let some ci := env.find? n | continue
    stack := stack ++ ci.type.getUsedConstants.toList ++ (ci.value?.map (·.getUsedConstants.toList) |>.getD [])
  while !stack.isEmpty do
    let c := stack.head!
    stack := stack.tail!
    if seen.contains c then continue
    seen := seen.insert c
    cs := cs.insert c
    let some cc := env.find? c | continue
    stack := stack ++ cc.type.getUsedConstants.toList
    if env.getModuleIdxFor? c == some modIdx && cc.isDefinition then
      stack := stack ++ (cc.value?.map (·.getUsedConstants.toList) |>.getD [])
  let mut rows : Array String := #[]
  let mut reds : Array String := #[]
  for c in cs.toList do
    let some m := isTCS env c | continue
    if m == modN then continue
    let some cinfo := env.find? c | continue
    unless cinfo.isDefinition do continue
    if isInstanceCore env c then continue
    let isM := (Match.Extension.getMatcherInfo? env c).isSome
    let st ← liftCoreM <| getReducibilityStatus c
    if !isM && st == .reducible then
      reds := reds.push s!"REDUCIBLE {c} | {m}"
      continue
    rows := rows.push s!"SEALROW {modN} | {c} | {m} | matcher={isM} | {repr st}"
  logInfo m!"MODULE {modN}: touched {ts.length}, constants {ours.size}, reached {cs.size}"
  for r in rows.qsort (· < ·) do logInfo m!"{r}"
  for r in reds.qsort (· < ·) do logInfo m!"{r}"

syntax (name := axsCmd) "#axs " ident "[" str,* "]" : command

/-- axioms of every touched top-level declaration of a module (private ones included) -/
@[command_elab axsCmd] def elabAxs : CommandElab := fun stx => do
  let modN := stx[1].getId
  let ts : List String := (stx[3].getSepArgs.map fun s => s.isStrLit?.getD "").toList
  let env ← getEnv
  let some modIdx := env.getModuleIdx? modN | throwError "no module {modN}"
  for t in ts do
    let mut found := false
    for (n, _) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
      if env.getModuleIdxFor? n == some modIdx then
        let s := userStr n
        if s == t || s.endsWith ("." ++ t) then
          found := true
          let axs ← liftCoreM <| collectAxioms n
          let axs := axs.qsort (fun a b => a.toString < b.toString)
          logInfo m!"AXIOMS {modN} | {s} | {axs.toList}"
    unless found do logWarning m!"AXIOMS-NOT-FOUND {t}"

#collect TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFind ["find?_range_and_lt"]
#axs TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFind ["find?_range_and_lt"]
#collect TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Closure ["PolyTimeComputable.comp'", "PolyTimeComputable.congr"]
#axs TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Closure ["PolyTimeComputable.comp'", "PolyTimeComputable.congr"]
#collect TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PublicKeyLemmas ["uexp_half_sub"]
#axs TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PublicKeyLemmas ["uexp_half_sub"]
#collect TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Sampling ["abs_uexp_sub_le", "statClose_one", "foldl_bits_eq", "two_pow_size_le_two_mul"]
#axs TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Sampling ["abs_uexp_sub_le", "statClose_one", "foldl_bits_eq", "two_pow_size_le_two_mul"]
#collect TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.Arithmetic ["natToList_mod_two_pow", "listToNat_natToList_zero_append", "natToList_zero_append_drop", "listToNat_replicate_true", "listToNat_replicate_false", "listToNat_mulStr", "subStr_self", "val_inv_natCast_zmod_zero_le", "ArithmeticFP.le_poly", "ArithmeticFP.prime_poly"]

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared/evidence-r2/ControlsUnsealed.source.txt =====

import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.Rabin
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.DiscreteLogHardcore
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.ElGamal
import TCSlib.Cryptography.ZeroKnowledge.ThreeColoring.ColZKLemmas
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.PublicKeyLemmas
open Complexity Turing TCSlib.Cryptography TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates NumberTheory

namespace S1Unsealed
-- C1 natToList by its body
example (k N : ℕ) : natToList k N = List.ofFn (natToBits k N) := rfl
-- C2 listToNat by its body
example (w : List Bool) : listToNat w = w.foldl (fun a c => 2 * a + if c then 1 else 0) 0 := rfl
-- C3 rejectBlocksL by its body
example (E : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred E] (k B T : ℕ) (r : List Bool) :
    rejectBlocksL E k B T r = (List.range T).findSome? fun t =>
      if E (listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k)) then some (listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k))
      else none := rfl
-- C4 StatClose by its body
example (X Y : Fin 2 → ℕ) (δ : ℝ) :
    StatClose X Y δ ↔ ∀ T : ℕ → Prop, |uprob (fun s => T (X s)) - uprob (fun t => T (Y t))| ≤ δ :=
  Iff.rfl
-- C5 uexp by its body
example (f : Fin 3 → ℝ) : uexp f = (∑ a, f a) / Fintype.card (Fin 3) := rfl
-- C6 PushesUniform by its body
example (π : Fin 2 → Fin 2) :
    HardcoreBit.PushesUniform π ↔ ∀ F : Fin 2 → ℝ, uexp (fun ω => F (π ω)) = uexp F := Iff.rfl
-- C7 PolyTimeComputable by its body
example (f : List Bool → List Bool) : PolyTimeComputable f ↔
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (C c : ℕ), M.ComputesFunInTime f fun n => C * (n + 1) ^ c := Iff.rfl
-- C8 sampleUnitL by its body
example (N k B T : ℕ) (r : List Bool) :
    sampleUnitL N k B T r = rejectBlocksL (fun v => v < N ∧ Nat.Coprime v N) k B T r := rfl
-- C9 subStr by its body
example (z : List Bool) : subStr z =
    natToList (pairFstD z).length (listToNat (pairFstD z) - listToNat (pairSndD z)) := rfl
-- C10 the repetition host's matcher against a local match on the same discriminant
example (o : Option ℕ) (a : ℕ → List Bool) (b : List Bool) :
    Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind.match_1 (fun _ => List Bool) o (fun i => a i) (fun _ => b) =
      (match o with | some i => a i | none => b) := rfl
-- C11 sampleBelowL by its body
example (m k B T : ℕ) (r : List Bool) : sampleBelowL m k B T r = (List.range T).findSome? fun t =>
    if listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k) < m then some (listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k))
    else none := rfl
-- C12 bitsToNat by its body
example (b : Fin 3 → Bool) :
    bitsToNat b = (List.ofFn b).foldl (fun a c => 2 * a + (if c then 1 else 0)) 0 := rfl
-- C13 mulStr by its body
example (z : List Bool) : mulStr z = natToList ((pairFstD z).length + (pairSndD z).length)
    (listToNat (pairFstD z) * listToNat (pairSndD z)) := rfl
end S1Unsealed

namespace S1PrimeControl
example (w : List Bool) : primeStr w = [decide (listToNat w).Prime] := rfl
end S1PrimeControl

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared/evidence-r2/check-census.py =====

"""G08-04 lexical regressions; run from the campaign root with python3 -I."""
from pathlib import Path
import runpy

root = Path.cwd()
gate = root / "briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared"
api = runpy.run_path(str(gate / "evidence/tools/sorrycensus.py"), run_name="census_api")
cases = [
    ("sorry", 1),
    ('"declaration uses \'sorry\'"', 0),
    ("/- outer /- sorry -/ sorry -/ sorry", 1),
    ("-- sorry\nsorry", 1),
    ('"escaped \\" sorry" sorry', 1),
    ('r##"sorry \\" sorry"## sorry', 1),
    ("«sorry» sorryAx sorry' A.sorry sorry", 1),
]
lines = []
for source, expected in cases:
    actual = api["count"](source)
    assert actual == expected, (source, actual, expected)
    lines.append(f"PASS {source!r}: {actual}")
lines.append(f"PASS {len(cases)} lexical regression cases")
(gate / "evidence-r2/census-regressions.log").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
print("\n".join(lines))

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared/evidence/tools/sorrycensus.py =====

"""Lexical sorry census outside nested comments, strings and quoted identifiers.

Usage: python3 -I sorrycensus.py <root> [--rev REV]. This is not elaboration.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import re
import subprocess

TOKEN = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.'])sorry(?![\w'])")
RAW_START = re.compile(r'r(#+)"')


def code_text(source):
    out, i, depth = [], 0, 0
    while i < len(source):
        if source.startswith("/-", i):
            depth += 1; out.append("  "); i += 2
        elif depth and source.startswith("-/", i):
            depth -= 1; out.append("  "); i += 2
        elif depth:
            out.append("\n" if source[i] == "\n" else " "); i += 1
        elif source.startswith("--", i):
            end = source.find("\n", i)
            end = len(source) if end < 0 else end
            out.append(" " * (end - i)); i = end
        elif source[i] == "«":
            end = source.find("»", i + 1)
            end = len(source) if end < 0 else end + 1
            out.append(" " * (end - i)); i = end
        else:
            raw = RAW_START.match(source, i)
            if raw:
                marker = '"' + raw.group(1)
                end = source.find(marker, raw.end())
                end = len(source) if end < 0 else end + len(marker)
                out.append("\n" * source[i:end].count("\n") + " "); i = end
            elif source[i] == '"':
                i += 1; out.append(" ")
                while i < len(source):
                    if source[i] == "\\":
                        i += 2
                    elif source[i] == '"':
                        i += 1; break
                    else:
                        if source[i] == "\n": out.append("\n")
                        i += 1
            else:
                out.append(source[i]); i += 1
    return "".join(out)


def count(source):
    return len(TOKEN.findall(code_text(source)))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("root", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--rev")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.rev:
        paths = subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "-C", str(args.root), "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", args.rev, "TCSlib"],
            text=True).splitlines()
        paths = [path for path in paths if path.endswith(".lean")]
    else:
        paths = [str(path.relative_to(args.root)) for path in (args.root / "TCSlib").rglob("*.lean")]
    total = 0
    for path in sorted(paths):
        source = subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "-C", str(args.root), "show", args.rev + ":" + path], text=True
        ) if args.rev else (args.root / path).read_text()
        number = count(source)
        if number:
            print(f"{number:4d} {path}"); total += number
    print(f"TOTAL {total}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared/evidence/tools/mkseal.py =====

"""mkseal.py SRC OUT NAMESFILE: whole-file seal, inserted after the first `open` line that follows the
file's (single) outer `namespace` line (or after that line if no `open` follows directly)."""
import sys
src, out, nf = sys.argv[1:4]
names = [l.strip() for l in open(nf) if l.strip()]
L = open(src, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
i = next(k for k, l in enumerate(L) if l.startswith('namespace '))
j = i + 1
while j < len(L) and not L[j].strip(): j += 1
ins = j if L[j].startswith('open ') else i
seal = ('-- S1 SEAL: the foreign TCSlib definitions collected from the elaborated terms of the touched '
        'declarations, plus matchers (PolyExpr.eval and glNeed left unsealed)')
if names:
    L.insert(ins + 1, seal + '\nattribute [local irreducible] ' + ' '.join('_root_.' + n for n in names))
open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(L))
print(len(names), 'names sealed after line', ins + 1)

## ===== briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared/evidence/tools/errdecl.py =====

"""errdecl.py <sealed.lean> <sealed.out> <touched.txt>: the declaration enclosing each error, and
whether it is touched."""
import re, sys
src, out, tf = sys.argv[1:4]
DECL = re.compile(r"^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?(?:(?:private|protected|noncomputable|nonrec)\s+)*"
                  r"(theorem|lemma|def|instance|structure|inductive|abbrev|class|example)\s*([^\s(:{\[]*)")
L = open(src, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
touched = {l.strip() for l in open(tf) if l.strip()}
starts = [(i + 1, m.group(2)) for i, l in enumerate(L) if (m := DECL.match(l))]
seen = set()
for l in open(out):
    m = re.match(r'.*?\.lean:(\d+):\d+: error', l)
    if not m: continue
    ln = int(m.group(1))
    d = max((s for s in starts if s[0] <= ln), default=(0, '?'))
    if d in seen: continue
    seen.add(d)
    print(f"line {ln}: decl `{d[1]}` (starts {d[0]}) touched={d[1] in touched}")

"""Compare each supplemental failing declaration's code with the checked base; python3 -I."""
from pathlib import Path
import ast
import hashlib
import json
import re
import subprocess

root = Path.cwd()
gate = root / "briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/gates/08-shared"
out = gate / "evidence-r2"
base = (out / "BASE.txt").read_text().strip()
head = (out / "HEAD.txt").read_text().strip()
summary = json.loads((out / "conservative-summary.json").read_text())
assert summary["head"] == head
# Reuse exactly the existing comment stripper without executing its CLI entry point.
tree = ast.parse((root / "briefs/pass-shelat-ch5-8/maintainer/tools/codeonly.py").read_text())
strip_def = next(node for node in tree.body if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == "strip")
scope = {}
exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[strip_def], type_ignores=[]), "codeonly.py:strip", "exec"), scope)
strip = scope["strip"]
decl = re.compile(r"^(?:@\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?(?:(?:private|protected|noncomputable|nonrec)\s+)*"
                  r"(?:theorem|lemma|def|instance|structure|inductive|abbrev|class|example)\s*([^\s(:{\[]*)")


def blocks(source):
    lines = source.splitlines()
    starts = [(i, m.group(1)) for i, line in enumerate(lines) if (m := decl.match(line))]
    result = []
    for (start, name), (end, _) in zip(starts, starts[1:] + [(len(lines), "")]):
        code = strip("\n".join(lines[start:end])).splitlines()
        # A removed following declaration can expose the outer `end` in this chunk.
        cut = next((i for i, line in enumerate(code[1:], 1)
                    if re.match(r"^(?:namespace|end|section|open|attribute|set_option|run_cmd)\b|^#", line)), len(code))
        result.append((name, start + 1, "\n".join(code[:cut])))
    return result


results = []
for row in summary["seal_results"]:
    module = row["module"]
    path = module.replace(".", "/") + ".lean"
    stem = Path(path).stem
    prefix = summary["probe_prefix"]
    probe = (out / "conservative" / (prefix + stem + ".source.txt")).read_text()
    seal_end = probe.splitlines().index("-- END IMPORT-CLOSURE SEAL") + 1
    log = (out / "logs" / (prefix + stem + ".log")).read_text()
    error_lines = [int(n) for n in re.findall(r"\.lean:(\d+):\d+: error", log)]
    assert len(error_lines) == row["diagnostics"]
    assert all(n > seal_end for n in error_lines), (module, error_lines, seal_end)
    a = blocks(subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", base + ":" + path], text=True))
    b = blocks(subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", head + ":" + path], text=True))
    for name in row["declarations"]:
        aa = [block for block in a if block[0] == name]
        bb = [block for block in b if block[0] == name]
        assert name and len(aa) == len(bb) == 1, (module, name, len(aa), len(bb))
        same = aa[0][2] == bb[0][2]
        results.append({"module": module, "declaration": name, "base_line": aa[0][1],
                        "head_line": bb[0][1], "comment_stripped_block_identical": same,
                        "base_code_sha256": hashlib.sha256(aa[0][2].encode()).hexdigest(),
                        "head_code_sha256": hashlib.sha256(bb[0][2].encode()).hexdigest()})
result = {"base": base, "head": head, "failing_declarations": len(results),
          "all_comment_stripped_blocks_identical": all(row["comment_stripped_block_identical"] for row in results),
          "seal_commands_no_diagnostics": True, "base_seal_rerun": False, "results": results}
(out / "conservative-failure-preservation.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))

/-

import TCSlib.Cryptography.OneWayFunctions.Amplification
import TCSlib.Cryptography.NumberTheory.Chebyshev
import TCSlib.Cryptography.NumberTheory.Units
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Sampling
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.Adversary
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Asymptotic.CollectionsHelpers
import TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.Arithmetic
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Prod

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Concrete lemmas for the factoring-based candidates

The concrete-layer content of the reductions of [PS10, §2.3–§2.4, §2.7] (Theorems 33.5,
36.3, 51.1), stated as exact inequalities at one security parameter in the style of
[Gar26] and consumed by `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.Factoring`:

* *conditioning* (lemma C1 of the chapter 2 inventory): the probability of an event on the
  uniform subtype `{a // E a}` is `Pr[E ∧ S] / Pr[E]`, and is at least
  `1 - (1 - Pr[S]) / δ` when `Pr[E] ≥ δ` — the step of [PS10, Theorem 33.5] turning an
  inverter of `f_mult` on uniform pairs into a factorer on uniform *prime* pairs;
* the *diagonal*: a uniform pair of elements of a finite type coincides with probability
  `1 / |γ|` (the switch from `Π_n × Π_n` to pairs of distinct primes);
* *random-position planting with a good set* (lemma C3): the one-call reduction of
  [PS10, Algorithm 37.4] (plant the challenge at a uniform position of a fresh tuple,
  `OneWay.yaoTry`) inverts `f` on a uniform *good* input with probability at least
  `(μ - (1 - Pr[G])^m) / m`, `μ` the success of the inverter of the direct product
  `prodFun f m` — the mirror of `OneWay.invProb_prodFun_le` [Gar26, Theorem 2.1] with the
  bad set replaced by the complement of the good set;
* the *tail bound* `(1 - 1/a)^{a k} ≤ e^{-k}` (lemma C8) and its instance
  `(1 - 1/(4n²))^{4n³} ≤ e^{-n}` [PS10, Claim 36.2], with `e^{-n} ≤ 2^{-n}`;
* the *prime-pair density* on `n`-bit strings and the identification of the uniform subtype
  of prime pairs with `Π_n × Π_n` (`primesPairEquiv`);
* the type `DistinctPrimes n` of pairs of distinct primes of `Π_n` (the restriction `p ≠ q`
  of the decision log "Rabin/RSA scope") with its string encoding, its `NeZero`/`Fact`
  instances and `Φ(pq) = (p−1)(q−1)` (moved here from `RSA.lean`, run-3 audit P7-6);
* *block rejection sampling* on coin lists (`rejectBlocksL`, run-3 audit P7-6): the one
  sampler behind the honest samplers of `Z_N^*`, `Z*_{Φ(N)}` and the restricted prime classes
  of [PS10, §2.9–§2.12], with its closeness lemma `statClose_rejectBlocksL` (lemma C4 on
  coin lists).

## Main definitions

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.primesPairEquiv` — prime pairs of `n`-bit strings as
  `Π_n × Π_n`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.DistinctPrimes` — pairs of distinct primes of `Π_n` (the
  index distribution of the factoring assumption and of the RSA/Rabin moduli), with
  `DistinctPrimes.default`, `encodeDistinctPrimes`, `decodeDistinctPrimes`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.rejectBlocksL` — block rejection sampling on a coin list.

## Main results

* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.uprob_and_eq_mul_subtype`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.one_sub_div_le_uprob_subtype` (C1),
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.uprob_le_uprob_subtype_add`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.uprob_subtype_prod_eq` — conditioning on an event.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.uprob_diag` — the diagonal of a uniform pair.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.invProb_prodFun_le_plant` (C3) — random-position
  planting with a good set [PS10, Algorithm 37.4, Theorem 36.3].
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.one_sub_one_div_pow_le_exp_neg` (C8),
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.claim_36_2` [PS10, Claim 36.2],
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.exp_neg_le_half_pow`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.one_div_le_uprob_prime_pair_bits`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.one_div_card_primes_le` — density facts in the forms
  the reductions use.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.decodeDistinctPrimes_encode`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.DistinctPrimes.isEmpty_of_lt` — the encoding of distinct
  prime pairs is lossless; `Π_n` has no two distinct primes for `n < 2`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.DistinctPrimes.totient_mul`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.DistinctPrimes.one_lt_totient` — `Φ(pq) = (p−1)(q−1) ≥ 2`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.rejectBlocksL_spec`,
  `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.statClose_rejectBlocksL` — accepted values satisfy the
  test; the total sampler is within `(1 − Pr[E])^T` of uniform on `E`.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.rejectBlocksL_eq_find?` — block rejection sampling as a
  search followed by the value read.
* `TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates.polyTimeComputable_rejectBlocksL` — block rejection sampling
  is polynomial-time (host H15; statement only, its proof is an open fill).

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (§2.3.1–§2.3.2, Theorem 33.5, Algorithm 33.6; §2.4.2, Claim 36.2, Theorem 36.3,
  Algorithm 37.4; §2.7, Theorem 51.1; Theorems 52.3, 53.2, 61.7 and 63.10, the samplers of
  block rejection sampling.)
* [Gar26] S. Garg, *A Course in Theory of Cryptography*, lecture notes, UC Berkeley,
  draft of 22 January 2026, §2.3 (Theorem 2.1 and Figure 2.2: planting at a uniform
  position).
-/
