String) do
    let ns := (catalog[spelling]?).getD #[]
    unless ns.size == 1 do throwError "seal name not found or ambiguous: {spelling}"
    let n := ns[0]!
    let before ← Lean.Elab.Command.liftCoreM <| Lean.getReducibilityStatus n
    if before == .irreducible then
      already := already + 1
    else
      let id := Lean.mkIdent n
      Lean.Elab.Command.elabCommand (← `(command| attribute [local irreducible] $id:ident))
      active := active + 1
    let status ← Lean.Elab.Command.liftCoreM <| Lean.getReducibilityStatus n
    unless status == .irreducible do throwError "seal not installed: {n}"
  Lean.logInfo m!"SUPPLEMENT-SEAL active={active} already={already}"
-- END IMPORT-CLOSURE SEAL


/-! ## Conditioning on an event (lemma C1) -/

section Conditioning

variable {α ρ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ρ]

/-- **Conditioning, multiplicative form**: `Pr[E ∧ S] = Pr[E] · Pr[S | E]`, where `Pr[S | E]`
is the probability of `S` under the uniform distribution on the subtype `{a // E a}`
(lemma C1 of the chapter 2 inventory, [PS10, proof of Theorem 33.5]: "`A'` feeds `A` a
uniformly distributed input … and replaces `xy` with `z` if both are prime"). -/
theorem uprob_and_eq_mul_subtype (E S : α → Prop) [DecidablePred E] :
    uprob (fun a => E a ∧ S a) = uprob E * uprob (fun z : {a // E a} => S z.1) := by
  simp only [uprob_def]
  rw [← Nat.card_congr (Equiv.subtypeSubtypeEquivSubtypeInter E S)]
  rcases (Fintype.card {a // E a}).eq_zero_or_pos with h0 | hpos
  · haveI : IsEmpty {a // E a} := Fintype.card_eq_zero_iff.mp h0
    have h1 : Nat.card {z : {a // E a} // S z.1} = 0 := Nat.card_of_isEmpty
    have h2 : Nat.card {a // E a} = 0 := Nat.card_of_isEmpty
    rw [h1, h2]
    simp
  · rw [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card (α := {a // E a})]
    have hc : (Fintype.card {a // E a} : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hpos.ne'
    field_simp

/-- **Conditioning, lower bound** (lemma C1, [PS10, proof of Theorem 33.5, the union
bound]): if `Pr[E] ≥ δ > 0` then `Pr[S | E] ≥ 1 - (1 - Pr[S]) / δ`. With `Pr[E] ≥ 1/(4n²)`
and `1 - Pr[S] ≤ 1/(8(n+1)²)` this gives `Pr[S | E] ≥ 1/2`.

**Proof sketch.** `Pr[S] ≤ Pr[E ∧ S] + Pr[¬E] = Pr[E]·Pr[S | E] + 1 - Pr[E]`, so
`Pr[E]·(1 - Pr[S | E]) ≤ 1 - Pr[S]`; divide by `Pr[E] ≥ δ`. -/
theorem one_sub_div_le_uprob_subtype (E S : α → Prop) [DecidablePred E] {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hE : δ ≤ uprob E) : 1 - (1 - uprob S) / δ ≤ uprob (fun z : {a // E a} => S z.1) := by
  haveI : Nonempty α := by
    by_contra h
    rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h
    have h0 : uprob E = 0 := by
      rw [uprob_def]
      simp
    linarith
  have hES := uprob_and_eq_mul_subtype E S
  have hsplit : uprob S ≤ uprob (fun a => E a ∧ S a) + uprob (fun a => ¬ E a) := by
    refine (uprob_mono ?_).trans (uprob_or_le _ _)
    intro a ha
    by_cases hEa : E a
    · exact Or.inl ⟨hEa, ha⟩
    · exact Or.inr hEa
  rw [uprob_not, hES] at hsplit
  have hEpos : 0 < uprob E := lt_of_lt_of_le hδ hE
  have h1 : 1 - uprob (fun z : {a // E a} => S z.1) ≤ (1 - uprob S) / uprob E := by
    rw [le_div_iff₀ hEpos]
    nlinarith
  have h2 : (1 - uprob S) / uprob E ≤ (1 - uprob S) / δ :=
    div_le_div_of_nonneg_left (by linarith [uprob_le_one S]) hδ hE
  linarith

/-- **Dropping a conditioning**: `Pr[S] ≤ Pr[S | E] + Pr[¬E]` (the switch from the uniform
pair of primes `Π_n × Π_n` to the uniform pair of *distinct* primes, whose complement — the
diagonal — has probability `1/|Π_n|`). -/
theorem uprob_le_uprob_subtype_add (E S : α → Prop) [DecidablePred E] :
    uprob S ≤ uprob (fun z : {a // E a} => S z.1) + uprob (fun a => ¬ E a) := by
  have hES := uprob_and_eq_mul_subtype E S
  have hsplit : uprob S ≤ uprob (fun a => E a ∧ S a) + uprob (fun a => ¬ E a) := by
    refine (uprob_mono ?_).trans (uprob_or_le _ _)
    intro a ha
    by_cases hEa : E a
    · exact Or.inl ⟨hEa, ha⟩
    · exact Or.inr hEa
  have h1 : uprob (fun a => E a ∧ S a) ≤ uprob (fun z : {a // E a} => S z.1) := by
    rw [hES]
    exact mul_le_of_le_one_left (uprob_nonneg _) (uprob_le_one _)
  linarith

/-- Conditioning on the first coordinate of a product: the uniform subtype `{a // E a}` with
independent auxiliary coins `ρ` is the uniform subtype of pairs whose first coordinate
satisfies `E` (relabelling by `Equiv.prodSubtypeFstEquivSubtypeProd`). -/
theorem uprob_subtype_prod_eq (E : α → Prop) [DecidablePred E] (S : α × ρ → Prop) :
    uprob (fun z : {a // E a} × ρ => S (z.1.1, z.2)) =
      uprob (fun z : {w : α × ρ // E w.1} => S z.1) :=
  uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodSubtypeFstEquivSubtypeProd (p := E)).symm fun z => S z.1

/-- **The diagonal**: a uniform pair of elements of a nonempty finite type consists of equal
elements with probability `1 / |γ|`. -/
theorem uprob_diag {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] [Nonempty γ] :
    uprob (fun z : γ × γ => z.2 = z.1) = 1 / Fintype.card γ := by
  rw [uprob_prod]
  simp only [uprob_eq_one_div_card]
  exact uexp_const _

end Conditioning

/-! ## Random-position planting with a good set (lemma C3) -/

section Planting

variable {α β ρ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ρ] {m : ℕ}

/-- **Random-position planting with a good set** (lemma C3 of the chapter 2 inventory; the
concrete content of [PS10, Theorem 36.3] with the one-call reduction of
[PS10, Algorithm 37.4] planting the challenge at a *uniform* position): if `B` inverts the
direct product `prodFun f m` with probability `μ`, then either every coordinate of the
uniform tuple is outside the good set `G` (probability `(1 - Pr[G])^m`) or the one-call
reduction `yaoTry f B` (plant `f x` at the uniform position `i` of a fresh tuple, call `B`,
return the `i`-th answer) inverts `f(x)` for a uniform `x` lying in `G`:
`μ ≤ (1 - Pr[G])^m + m · Pr_{x, i, xs, r}[x ∈ G ∧ f(yaoTry f B (f x) (i, xs, r)) = f x]`.
Mirror of `OneWay.invProb_prodFun_le` [Gar26, Theorem 2.1] with the bad set replaced by
`¬G`.

**Deviation:** [PS10, Algorithm 37.4] plants at the first prime pair and tests primality;
planting at a uniform position needs no primality test (the text's exercise, p. 37).

**Proof sketch.** Success of `B` on `(xs, r)` means that every `xs i` is outside `G` or that
some position `i` has `xs i ∈ G` and the `i`-th answer inverts `f (xs i)`
(`uprob_mono`, `uprob_or_le`, `uprob_exists_le`). The first event has probability
`(1 - Pr[G])^m` (`uprob_fst`, `OneWay.uprob_pi_forall`, `uprob_not`). For fixed `i`, planting
a fresh uniform `x` at position `i` leaves the tuple uniform (`OneWay.uprob_update`,
`OneWay.prodFun_update`), which rewrites the `i`-th event as the planted experiment; summing
over `i` makes the position uniform (`OneWay.sum_uprob_eq_card_mul`), and a relabelling of
the coin space finishes. -/
theorem invProb_prodFun_le_plant [Nonempty α] [Nonempty ρ] (f : α → β)
    (B : (Fin m → β) → ρ → (Fin m → α)) (G : α → Prop) :
    invProb (prodFun f m) B ≤ (1 - uprob G) ^ m +
      m * uprob (fun z : α × (Fin m × ((Fin m → α) × ρ)) =>
        G z.1 ∧ f (yaoTry f B (f z.1) z.2) = f z.1) := by
  classical
  rw [invProb_def]
  calc uprob (fun z : (Fin m → α) × ρ =>
        prodFun f m (B (prodFun f m z.1) z.2) = prodFun f m z.1)
      ≤ uprob (fun z : (Fin m → α) × ρ => (∀ i, ¬ G (z.1 i)) ∨
          ∃ i ∈ (univ : Finset (Fin m)),
            G (z.1 i) ∧ f (B (prodFun f m z.1) z.2 i) = f (z.1 i)) := by
        apply uprob_mono
        rintro ⟨xs, r⟩ h
        by_cases hall : ∀ i, ¬ G (xs i)
        · exact Or.inl hall
        · push_neg at hall
          obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hall
          have hfi := congrFun h i
          rw [OneWay.prodFun_apply, OneWay.prodFun_apply] at hfi
          exact Or.inr ⟨i, mem_univ _, hi, hfi⟩
    _ ≤ uprob (fun z : (Fin m → α) × ρ => ∀ i, ¬ G (z.1 i)) +
          ∑ i, uprob (fun z : (Fin m → α) × ρ =>
            G (z.1 i) ∧ f (B (prodFun f m z.1) z.2 i) = f (z.1 i)) :=
        (uprob_or_le _ _).trans (add_le_add_left (uprob_exists_le _ _) _)
    _ ≤ _ := by
        apply add_le_add
        · rw [uprob_fst (fun xs : Fin m → α => ∀ i, ¬ G (xs i)),
            uprob_pi_forall (ι := Fin m) (fun x => ¬ G x), uprob_not, Fintype.card_fin]
        · have hplant : ∀ i, uprob (fun z : (Fin m → α) × ρ =>
              G (z.1 i) ∧ f (B (prodFun f m z.1) z.2 i) = f (z.1 i)) =
              uprob (fun z : α × ((Fin m → α) × ρ) =>
                G z.1 ∧ f (yaoTry f B (f z.1) (i, z.2)) = f z.1) := by
            intro i
            rw [← uprob_update i (fun xs r =>
              G (xs i) ∧ f (B (prodFun f m xs) r i) = f (xs i))]
            apply uprob_congr
            rintro ⟨x, xs, r⟩
            simp [yaoTry_eq, prodFun_update]
          simp only [hplant]
          rw [sum_uprob_eq_card_mul, Fintype.card_fin]
          let e : α × (Fin m × ((Fin m → α) × ρ)) ≃ Fin m × (α × ((Fin m → α) × ρ)) :=
            { toFun := fun z => (z.2.1, (z.1, z.2.2))
              invFun := fun z => (z.2.1, (z.1, z.2.2))
              left_inv := fun _ => rfl
              right_inv := fun _ => rfl }
          rw [← uprob_comp_equiv e]
          exact le_rfl

end Planting

/-! ## Tail bounds (lemma C8, Claim 36.2) -/

/-- **Tail bound** (lemma C8 of the chapter 2 inventory): `(1 - 1/a)^{a·k} ≤ e^{-k}` for
`a ≥ 1` (the inequality `1 - t ≤ e^{-t}` raised to the power `a·k`,
`Real.one_sub_div_pow_le_exp_neg`). -/
theorem one_sub_one_div_pow_le_exp_neg (a k : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    (1 - 1 / (a : ℝ)) ^ (a * k) ≤ Real.exp (-(k : ℝ)) := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with rfl | hk
  · simp
  have h := Real.one_sub_div_pow_le_exp_neg (n := a * k) (t := (k : ℝ))
    (by push_cast; nlinarith [(by exact_mod_cast ha : (1 : ℝ) ≤ a), (by exact_mod_cast hk : (0 : ℝ) < k)])
  have heq : (1 - (k : ℝ) / ((a * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) = 1 - 1 / (a : ℝ) := by
    have hk' : (k : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hk.ne'
    have ha' : (a : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast ha.ne'
    push_cast
    field_simp
  rw [heq] at h
  exact h

/-- **Claim 36.2** [PS10, (36.2)]: `(1 - 1/(4n²))^{4n³} = ((1 - 1/(4n²))^{4n²})^n ≤ e^{-n}`:
with `4n³` pairs of random `n`-bit numbers, the probability that none of them is a pair of
primes is at most `e^{-n}` (given the density `1/(4n²)` of prime pairs). -/
theorem claim_36_2 (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    (1 - 1 / (4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) ^ (4 * n ^ 3) ≤ Real.exp (-(n : ℝ)) := by
  have h := one_sub_one_div_pow_le_exp_neg (4 * n ^ 2) n (by positivity)
  have hexp : 4 * n ^ 2 * n = 4 * n ^ 3 := by ring
  rw [hexp] at h
  push_cast at h
  exact h

/-- `e^{-n} ≤ (1/2)^n` (the negligible form of the tail bounds, `negligible_two_pow_neg`). -/
theorem exp_neg_le_half_pow (n : ℕ) : Real.exp (-(n : ℝ)) ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n := by
  have h1 : Real.exp (-(n : ℝ)) = Real.exp (-1) ^ n := by
    rw [← Real.exp_nat_mul]; congr 1; ring
  rw [h1]
  apply pow_le_pow_left₀ (Real.exp_pos _).le
  rw [Real.exp_neg]
  have := Real.add_one_le_exp (1 : ℝ)
  rw [inv_eq_one_div, div_le_div_iff₀ (Real.exp_pos 1) (by norm_num)]
  linarith

/-- **Claim 36.2, negligible form**: `(1 - 1/(4n²))^{4n³} ≤ 2^{-n}`. -/
theorem claim_36_2_half_pow (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    (1 - 1 / (4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2)) ^ (4 * n ^ 3) ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ n :=
  (claim_36_2 n hn).trans (exp_neg_le_half_pow n)

/-! ## Prime pairs of bit strings -/

/-- **Prime-pair density on bit strings** [PS10, proof of Theorem 33.5]: for `n ≥ 2`, a
uniform pair of `n`-bit strings reads (`bitsToNat`) as a pair of primes with probability at
least `1/(4n²)` (`NumberTheory.one_div_le_uprob_prime_pair` transported along
`bitsEquiv`). -/
theorem one_div_le_uprob_prime_pair_bits (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    1 / (4 * (n : ℝ) ^ 2) ≤
      uprob (fun z : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) =>
        (bitsToNat z.1).Prime ∧ (bitsToNat z.2).Prime) := by
  have h := one_div_le_uprob_prime_pair n hn
  rw [← uprob_comp_equiv (Equiv.prodCongr (bitsEquiv n) (bitsEquiv n))] at h
  simpa using h

/-- The uniform subtype of prime pairs of `n`-bit strings is `Π_n × Π_n`: read each string as
a number (`bitsEquiv`) and split the conjunction (`Equiv.subtypeProdEquivProd`). -/
noncomputable def primesPairEquiv (n : ℕ) :
    {z : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) // (bitsToNat z.1).Prime ∧ (bitsToNat z.2).Prime} ≃
      Primes n × Primes n :=
  (Equiv.subtypeEquiv (Equiv.prodCongr (bitsEquiv n) (bitsEquiv n)) (fun z => by simp)).trans
    Equiv.subtypeProdEquivProd

/-- The components of `primesPairEquiv` are the numbers read from the two strings. -/
@[simp] theorem primesPairEquiv_apply_val (n : ℕ)
    (z : {z : (Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → Bool) // (bitsToNat z.1).Prime ∧ (bitsToNat z.2).Prime}) :
    ((primesPairEquiv n z).1.1 : ℕ) = bitsToNat z.1.1 ∧
      ((primesPairEquiv n z).2.1 : ℕ) = bitsToNat z.1.2 := by
  simp [primesPairEquiv, Equiv.subtypeProdEquivProd]

/-- `1/|Π_n| ≤ 2n/2^n` for `n ≥ 2` (`NumberTheory.two_pow_le_two_mul_card_primes`): the
probability that two independent uniform primes coincide is negligible. -/
theorem one_div_card_primes_le (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    1 / (Fintype.card (Primes n) : ℝ) ≤ 2 * n / 2 ^ n := by
  have h := two_pow_le_two_mul_card_primes n hn
  have h' : (2 : ℝ) ^ n ≤ 2 * n * Fintype.card (Primes n) := by exact_mod_cast h
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < Fintype.card (Primes n) := by
    have : 0 < Fintype.card (Primes n) := by
      by_contra h0
      push_neg at h0
      have : Fintype.card (Primes n) = 0 := by omega
      rw [this, mul_zero] at h
      exact absurd h (not_le.mpr (Nat.two_pow_pos n))
    exact_mod_cast this
  rw [div_le_div_iff₀ hpos (by positivity), one_mul]
  linarith

/-! ## Pairs of distinct primes -/

/-- Pairs of **distinct** primes of `Π_n`: the index distribution of the factoring
assumption and of the RSA/Rabin moduli `N = pq` (decision log "Rabin/RSA scope": `p ≠ q`). -/
abbrev DistinctPrimes (n : ℕ) : Type := {z : Primes n × Primes n // (z.1.1 : ℕ) ≠ z.2.1}

namespace DistinctPrimes

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The first prime `p`. -/
def p (z : DistinctPrimes n) : ℕ := z.1.1.1

/-- The defining equation of `DistinctPrimes.p`: `z.p` is the value of the first prime of the
pair, `z.p = ((z.1.1 : Fin (2^n)) : ℕ)`. -/
theorem p_eq (z : DistinctPrimes n) : z.p = ((z.1.1 : Fin (2 ^ n)) : ℕ) := rfl

/-- The second prime `q`. -/
def q (z : DistinctPrimes n) : ℕ := z.1.2.1

/-- The defining equation of `DistinctPrimes.q`: `z.q` is the value of the second prime of the
pair, `z.q = ((z.1.2 : Fin (2^n)) : ℕ)`. -/
theorem q_eq (z : DistinctPrimes n) : z.q = ((z.1.2 : Fin (2 ^ n)) : ℕ) := rfl

/-- `p` is prime. -/
theorem p_prime (z : DistinctPrimes n) : z.p.Prime := z.1.1.2

/-- `q` is prime. -/
theorem q_prime (z : DistinctPrimes n) : z.q.Prime := z.1.2.2

/-- `p < 2^n`. -/
theorem p_lt (z : DistinctPrimes n) : z.p < 2 ^ n := z.1.1.1.2

/-- `q < 2^n`. -/
theorem q_lt (z : DistinctPrimes n) : z.q < 2 ^ n := z.1.2.1.2

/-- `p ≠ q`. -/
theorem p_ne_q (z : DistinctPrimes n) : z.p ≠ z.q := z.2

/-- The modulus `N = pq < 2^{2n}`. -/
theorem mul_lt (z : DistinctPrimes n) : z.p * z.q < 2 ^ (2 * n) := by
  rw [two_mul]; exact mul_lt_two_pow_add z.p_lt z.q_lt

/-! ### Instances and the totient (moved from `RSA.lean`, run-3 audit P7-6) -/

/-- The modulus `pq` is nonzero. -/
instance neZero_mul (z : DistinctPrimes n) : NeZero (z.p * z.q) :=
  ⟨mul_ne_zero z.p_prime.ne_zero z.q_prime.ne_zero⟩

/-- `Φ(pq)` is nonzero. -/
instance neZero_totient (z : DistinctPrimes n) : NeZero (Nat.totient (z.p * z.q)) :=
  ⟨(Nat.totient_pos.2 (NeZero.pos _)).ne'⟩

/-- `p` is prime (as a `Fact`). -/
instance fact_p_prime (z : DistinctPrimes n) : Fact z.p.Prime := ⟨z.p_prime⟩

/-- `q` is prime (as a `Fact`). -/
instance fact_q_prime (z : DistinctPrimes n) : Fact z.q.Prime := ⟨z.q_prime⟩

/-- `Φ(pq) = (p−1)(q−1)` for a pair of distinct primes [PS10, p. 47]. -/
theorem totient_mul (z : DistinctPrimes n) : Nat.totient (z.p * z.q) = (z.p - 1) * (z.q - 1) :=
  totient_prime_mul_prime z.p_prime z.q_prime z.p_ne_q

/-- `Φ(pq) ≥ 2`: one of two distinct primes is at least `3`. -/
theorem one_lt_totient (z : DistinctPrimes n) : 1 < Nat.totient (z.p * z.q) := by
  rw [z.totient_mul]
  have hp := z.p_prime.two_le
  have hq := z.q_prime.two_le
  have hne := z.p_ne_q
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge 2 z.p with h | h
  · calc 1 < 2 * 1 := by norm_num
      _ ≤ (z.p - 1) * (z.q - 1) := Nat.mul_le_mul (by omega) (by omega)
  · have h2 : z.p = 2 := by omega
    have h3 : 3 ≤ z.q := by omega
    calc 1 < 1 * 2 := by norm_num
      _ ≤ (z.p - 1) * (z.q - 1) := Nat.mul_le_mul (by omega) (by omega)

/-- A pair of distinct primes is determined by `(p, q)`. -/
theorem ext {z w : DistinctPrimes n} (hp : z.p = w.p) (hq : z.q = w.q) : z = w := by
  rcases z with ⟨⟨⟨⟨p, hp'⟩, hpp⟩, ⟨⟨q, hq'⟩, hqq⟩⟩, hne⟩
  rcases w with ⟨⟨⟨⟨p', _⟩, _⟩, ⟨⟨q', _⟩, _⟩⟩, _⟩
  simp only [DistinctPrimes.p, DistinctPrimes.q] at hp hq
  subst hp hq
  rfl

/-- `Π_n` has no two distinct primes for `n < 2`. -/
theorem isEmpty_of_lt (hn : n < 2) : IsEmpty (DistinctPrimes n) := by
  refine ⟨fun z => ?_⟩
  have h1 := z.p_prime.two_le
  have h2 := z.q_prime.two_le
  have h3 := z.p_lt
  have h4 := z.q_lt
  have h5 := z.p_ne_q
  interval_cases n <;> omega

/-- The pair `(2, 3)` for `n ≥ 2` (the default element of the collection's domain). -/
def default (hn : 2 ≤ n) : DistinctPrimes n :=
  ⟨(⟨⟨2, lt_of_lt_of_le (by norm_num) ((Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hn).trans_eq' rfl)⟩,
      Nat.prime_two⟩,
    ⟨⟨3, lt_of_lt_of_le (by norm_num) ((Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hn).trans_eq' rfl)⟩,
      Nat.prime_three⟩), (by norm_num : (2 : ℕ) ≠ 3)⟩

/-- The first prime of the default pair is `2`: `(DistinctPrimes.default hn).p = 2`. -/
theorem default_p (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (DistinctPrimes.default hn).p = 2 := rfl

/-- The second prime of the default pair is `3`: `(DistinctPrimes.default hn).q = 3`. -/
theorem default_q (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (DistinctPrimes.default hn).q = 3 := rfl

end DistinctPrimes

/-! ### Encoding pairs of distinct primes -/

/-- Decode `⟨a, b⟩` as a pair of distinct primes of `Π_m`: both components must be `m`-bit
strings (`decodeFin`) reading as distinct primes; anything else is a failure. -/
def decodeDistinctPrimes (m : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : Option (DistinctPrimes m) :=
  match decodeFin m (pairFstD w), decodeFin m (pairSndD w) with
  | some a, some b =>
    if h : (bitsToNat a).Prime ∧ (bitsToNat b).Prime ∧ bitsToNat a ≠ bitsToNat b then
      some ⟨(⟨⟨bitsToNat a, bitsToNat_lt a⟩, h.1⟩, ⟨⟨bitsToNat b, bitsToNat_lt b⟩, h.2.1⟩), h.2.2⟩
    else none
  | _, _ => none

/-- Encode a pair of distinct primes of `Π_m` as `⟨p, q⟩` with `m`-bit numerals. -/
def encodeDistinctPrimes (m : ℕ) (z : DistinctPrimes m) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (natToList m z.p) (natToList m z.q)

/-- The defining equation of `encodeDistinctPrimes`:
`encodeDistinctPrimes m z = ⟨⟦p⟧_m, ⟦q⟧_m⟩`, the pair of the `m`-bit numerals of the two primes. -/
theorem encodeDistinctPrimes_eq (m : ℕ) (z : DistinctPrimes m) :
    encodeDistinctPrimes m z = pairEncode (natToList m z.p) (natToList m z.q) := rfl

/-- Decoding inverts encoding. -/
theorem decodeDistinctPrimes_encode (m : ℕ) (z : DistinctPrimes m) :
    decodeDistinctPrimes m (encodeDistinctPrimes m z) = some z := by
  unfold decodeDistinctPrimes encodeDistinctPrimes
  rw [natToList_eq, natToList_eq]
  simp only [pairFstD_pairEncode, pairSndD_pairEncode, decodeFin_ofFn,
    bitsToNat_natToBits z.p_lt, bitsToNat_natToBits z.q_lt]
  rw [dif_pos ⟨z.p_prime, z.q_prime, z.p_ne_q⟩]
  congr 1

/-- **Decoding is canonical**: a string that `decodeDistinctPrimes m` decodes to `z` is
`encodeDistinctPrimes m z` (the clause `Collection.encD_decD` of the factoring collection;
gate 03b, finding 1).

**Proof sketch.** Both components decode as `m`-bit strings `a`, `b`, so they are `List.ofFn a`,
`List.ofFn b` (`ofFn_of_decodeFin_eq_some`), the numerals of `p = bitsToNat a`, `q = bitsToNat b`
at width `m` (`natToList_length_listToNat`); the first is nonempty (`Π_m` has two distinct
primes only for `m ≥ 2`, `DistinctPrimes.isEmpty_of_lt`), so the string is the pair of its
components (`eq_pairEncode_of_pairFstD_ne`). -/
theorem encodeDistinctPrimes_of_decode {m : ℕ} {w : List Bool} {z : DistinctPrimes m}
    (h : decodeDistinctPrimes m w = some z) : encodeDistinctPrimes m z = w := by
  have hm : 2 ≤ m := by
    by_contra hm
    exact (DistinctPrimes.isEmpty_of_lt (not_le.1 hm)).false z
  have hnum : ∀ a : Fin m → Bool, natToList m (bitsToNat a) = List.ofFn a := fun a => by
    have := natToList_length_listToNat (List.ofFn a)
    rwa [List.length_ofFn, ← bitsToNat_eq_listToNat] at this
  unfold decodeDistinctPrimes at h
  rcases ha : decodeFin m (pairFstD w) with _ | a <;> rcases hb : decodeFin m (pairSndD w) with _ | b <;>
    simp only [ha, hb, reduceCtorEq] at h
  split_ifs at h with hc
  obtain rfl := Option.some.inj h
  have hne : pairFstD w ≠ [] := fun h0 => by
    have := length_eq_of_decodeFin_eq_some ha
    rw [h0, List.length_nil] at this
    omega
  show pairEncode (natToList m (bitsToNat a)) (natToList m (bitsToNat b)) = w
  rw [hnum, hnum, ofFn_of_decodeFin_eq_some ha, ofFn_of_decodeFin_eq_some hb]
  exact (eq_pairEncode_of_pairFstD_ne hne).symm

/-! ## Block rejection sampling on coin lists (run-3 audit P7-6) -/

/-- **Block rejection sampling** on a coin list, the common shape of the honest samplers of
the candidates [PS10, Theorem 53.2 (`Z_N^*`, `Z*_{Φ(N)}`), Theorem 61.7, Theorem 63.10 (Blum
primes), Theorem 52.3 (`Z_q`)]: `T` trials, trial `t` reading the first `k` bits of the
`t`-th block of `B` bits of `r` as a number `v` (`listToNat`), accepted iff `E v`; `none` if
every trial is rejected. With `k ≤ B` and `r` uniform, the `T` values are independent and
uniform below `2^k`, so the output is `firstHit E` on `Fin (2^k)` (`statClose_rejectBlocksL`).
Repair (run-3 audit P7-6): the one sampler behind `sampleUnitL` (RSA, Rabin) and
`samplePrimePL` (Rabin); `sampleBelowL` (discrete log) has the same shape. -/
def rejectBlocksL (E : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred E] (k B T : ℕ) (r : List Bool) : Option ℕ :=
  (List.range T).findSome? fun t =>
    if E (listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k)) then some (listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k))
    else none

/-- Block rejection sampling unfolded: `rejectBlocksL E k B T r` is the first `some v` over
`t ∈ [0, T)` (`List.findSome?` over `List.range T`) with `v` the number read from the first `k`
bits of the `t`-th block of `B` bits of `r`, kept iff `E v`. -/
theorem rejectBlocksL_eq (E : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred E] (k B T : ℕ) (r : List Bool) :
    rejectBlocksL E k B T r = (List.range T).findSome? fun t =>
      if E (listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k)) then some (listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k))
      else none :=
  rfl

/-- **Block rejection sampling as a search followed by the value read**: `rejectBlocksL E k B T r`
is the first trial `t < T` whose value `v_t = ⟦(r.drop (t B)).take k⟧` passes `E`, mapped to
`v_t`:
`rejectBlocksL E k B T r = ((List.range T).find? fun t => decide (E v_t)).map fun t => v_t`
(core `List.findSome?_guard`, `List.map_findSome?`, `Option.guard_apply`). -/
theorem rejectBlocksL_eq_find? (E : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred E] (k B T : ℕ) (r : List Bool) :
    rejectBlocksL E k B T r =
      ((List.range T).find? fun t => decide (E (listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k)))).map
        fun t => listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k) := by
  rw [rejectBlocksL_eq, ← List.findSome?_guard, List.map_findSome?]
  congr 1
  funext t
  rw [Function.comp_apply, Option.guard_apply]
  by_cases ht : E (listToNat ((r.drop (t * B)).take k))
  · rw [if_pos ht, decide_eq_true ht, if_pos rfl, Option.map_some]
  · rw [if_neg ht, decide_eq_false ht, if_neg Bool.false_ne_true, Option.map_none]

/-- An accepted value satisfies the test and is below `2^k` (it is read from at most `k`
bits, `listToNat_lt_two_pow`). -/
theorem rejectBlocksL_spec {E : ℕ → Prop} [DecidablePred E] {k B T : ℕ} {r : List Bool} {v : ℕ}
    (h : rejectBlocksL E k B T r = some v) : E v ∧ v < 2 ^ k := by
  unfold rejectBlocksL at h
  rw [List.findSome?_eq_some_iff] at h
  obtain ⟨_, t, _, _, ht, _⟩ := h
  split_ifs at ht with hc
  rw [Option.some.injEq] at ht
  subst ht
  refine ⟨hc, lt_of_lt_of_le (listToNat_lt_two_pow _) ?_⟩
  exact Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (List.length_take_le _ _)

/-- **Block rejection sampling is polynomial-time** (host H15) [PS10, Theorems 52.3, 53.2, 61.7
and 63.10: "the domain is easy to sample"]. Let `E a v` be a test on a parameter `a` and a value
`v`, decided on words by a polynomial-time bit `acc`, so that `acc ⟨w, b⟩ = [E ⟦w⟧ ⟦b⟧]`. Take
polynomial-time words `par z` (the parameter), `kw z`, `bw z` and `tw z`, whose lengths are the
trial width `k`, the block length `B` and the trial count `T`, and `c z` (the coins). Then some
polynomial-time `g` computes the sampler `rejectBlocksL (E ⟦par z⟧) k B T (c z)`:
- `g z = []` when every trial is rejected;
- otherwise `g z` is nonempty, and its tail reads as the accepted value and has at most `k` bits.

That is, `(g z).tail.length ≤ k` and
`rejectBlocksL (E ⟦par z⟧) k B T (c z) = if g z = [] then none else some ⟦(g z).tail⟧`.
In particular `(rejectBlocksL …).getD 0 = ⟦(g z).tail⟧`, since `[].tail = []` reads as `0`
(`listToNat_nil`). The statement is existential: the trial loop that realizes it is internal,
and no consumer reads it.

**Deviation:** [PS10] samples these domains exactly, in expected polynomial time; here the
sampler is truncated to `T` trials (deviations register #15, `statClose_rejectBlocksL` carries
the statistical term), and the host states only the polynomial-time computability of that
truncated sampler on strings.

**Proof sketch.**
- **The loop.** The state is `⟨⟨⟨1^B, 1^k⟩, w⟩, ⟨1^T, r⟩⟩`, with `w = par z` and `r = c z`. One
  step keeps the header `⟨⟨1^B, 1^k⟩, w⟩`, drops one bit of the counter `1^T` and one block of
  `B` coins (`polyTimeComputable_tail`, `polyTimeComputable_pairDropPoly`). The trial word is
  the first `k` coins (`polyTimeComputable_pairTakePoly`). The test accepts iff the counter is
  nonempty and `acc ⟨w, trial word⟩` holds (`polyTimeComputable_isNil`, `polyTimeComputable_not`,
  `polyTimeComputable_and`, with the tests given explicitly). The payload is `true` followed by
  the trial word (`polyTimeComputable_prepend`). The start state is assembled from the given
  words (`polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly`, or `List.replicate` of the lengths, and
  `PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode`), and `g` is the loop on it, in applied form
  (`PolyTimeComputable.comp'`).
- **Polynomial time.** One step at most doubles the length (`|step x| ≤ 2|x| + 4`), and from the
  second step on the state is a well-formed pair that only shrinks
  (`StateLoop.length_pairFstD_add_pairSndD_le`), so every orbit point has length at most
  `2|x| + 4`. The repetition host `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind`, with `R = var` and
  orbit bound `2n + 4`, therefore makes the loop polynomial-time. Its `match` on the search
  result is split by `split` (its equation lemmas), never matched by definitional unfolding.
- **Correctness.** After `i` steps the state is `⟨h, ⟨1^T.drop i, r.drop (i B)⟩⟩` (induction on
  `i`, `List.drop_drop`), so trial `i` reads the `k`-bit prefix `v_i = ⟦(r.drop (i B)).take k⟧`
  of block `i`, and the test at step `i` is `i < T ∧ E ⟦w⟧ v_i` (`hspec`). The search over the
  first `|start| + 1 ≥ T` rounds is therefore the search over `[0, T)`
  (`IterateFind.find?_range_and_lt`), which is `rejectBlocksL` read as a search followed by its
  value (`rejectBlocksL_eq_find?`). If the search fails, `g z = []`; otherwise
  `g z = true :: trial word`, whose tail has at most `k` bits (`List.length_take_le`) and reads
  as the accepted value. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_rejectBlocksL (E : ℕ → ℕ → Prop) [∀ a, DecidablePred (E a)]
    {acc : List Bool → Bool} (hacc : PolyTimeComputable fun x => [acc x])
    (hspec : ∀ w b : List Bool, acc (pairEncode w b) = decide (E (listToNat w) (listToNat b)))
    {par kw bw tw c : List Bool → List Bool} (hpar : PolyTimeComputable par)
    (hkw : PolyTimeComputable kw) (hbw : PolyTimeComputable bw) (htw : PolyTimeComputable tw)
    (hc : PolyTimeComputable c) :
    ∃ g : List Bool → List Bool, PolyTimeComputable g ∧ ∀ z,
      (g z).tail.length ≤ (kw z).length ∧
      rejectBlocksL (E (listToNat (par z))) (kw z).length (bw z).length (tw z).length (c z) =
        if g z = [] then none else some (listToNat (g z).tail) := by
  sorry

/-- The position of bit `j < k` of block `t < T` in a string of `T · B` coins (`k ≤ B`):
`t · B + j`. -/
private def dla_blockPos {k B T : ℕ} (hkB : k ≤ B) (p : Fin T × Fin k) : Fin (T * B) :=
  ⟨p.1.val * B + p.2.val, by
    have h1 := p.1.2
    have h2 := p.2.2
    calc p.1.val * B + p.2.val < p.1.val * B + B := by omega
      _ = (p.1.val + 1) * B := by ring
      _ ≤ T * B := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ h1⟩

/-- Distinct (block, bit) pairs sit at distinct coin positions (`j < k ≤ B`). -/
private theorem dla_blockPos_injective {k B T : ℕ} (hkB : k ≤ B) :
    Function.Injective (dla_blockPos (T := T) hkB) := by
  rintro ⟨t, j⟩ ⟨t', j'⟩ h
  have h' : t.val * B + j.val = t'.val * B + j'.val := congrArg Fin.val h
  have hj := j.2
  have hj' := j'.2
  have hB : 0 < B := lt_of_lt_of_le (Nat.zero_lt_of_lt hj) hkB
  have ht : t.val = t'.val := by
    have e1 : (t.val * B + j.val) / B = t.val := by
      rw [Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_mul_div_right _ _ hB, Nat.div_eq_of_lt (by omega), zero_add]
    have e2 : (t'.val * B + j'.val) / B = t'.val := by
      rw [Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_mul_div_right _ _ hB, Nat.div_eq_of_lt (by omega), zero_add]
    rw [← e1, ← e2, h']
  have hj2 : j.val = j'.val := by rw [ht] at h'; omega
  rw [Fin.ext ht, Fin.ext hj2]

/-- The `k`-bit prefix of block `t` of a coin string, read off the list: for `t < T` and
`k ≤ B`, `((List.ofFn r).drop (t · B)).take k = List.ofFn (fun j => r (t · B + j))`. -/
private theorem dla_take_drop_ofFn {k B T : ℕ} (hkB : k ≤ B) (r : Fin (T * B) → Bool) (t : Fin T) :
    ((List.ofFn r).drop (t.val * B)).take k =
      List.ofFn (fun j : Fin k => r (dla_blockPos hkB (t, j))) := by
  have hlen : t.val * B + k ≤ T * B := by
    have := t.2
    calc t.val * B + k ≤ t.val * B + B := by omega
      _ = (t.val + 1) * B := by ring
      _ ≤ T * B := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ this
  apply List.ext_getElem
  · rw [List.length_take, List.length_drop, List.length_ofFn, List.length_ofFn]
    omega
  · intro j h1 h2
    rw [List.getElem_take, List.getElem_drop, List.getElem_ofFn, List.getElem_ofFn]
    rfl

/-- **Block rejection sampling is close to uniform on `E`** (lemma C4 of the chapter 2
inventory on coin lists; the sampling clauses of [PS10, Theorems 52.3, 53.2, 61.7, 63.10]):
for `k ≤ B`, a uniform coin string of `T · B` bits and a default `d < 2^k` with `E d`, the
total sampler `(rejectBlocksL E k B T r).getD d` is within `(1 − Pr_{v < 2^k}[E v])^T` of the
uniform element of `{v < 2^k | E v}`. Repair (run-3 audit P7-6): stated once here instead of
in each consumer.

**Proof sketch.** For `r = List.ofFn r'`, `(r.drop (t·B)).take k = List.ofFn (π_t r')` where
`π_t r'` is the `k`-bit prefix of block `t` (`List.ext_get`, `List.getElem_take`,
`List.getElem_drop`, `List.getElem_ofFn`; the length is `k` since `t < T` and `k ≤ B`), so
`rejectBlocksL E k B T r = (firstHit (fun x : Fin (2^k) => E x) (fun t => bitsEquiv k (π_t r'))).map Fin.val`
(`List.map_coe_finRange`, `List.findSome?_map`, `bitsToNat_eq_listToNat`, `bitsEquiv_val`) and
`(·).getD d = Fin.val ((firstHit …).getD ⟨d, hdk⟩)` (`Option.getD_map`). The map
`r' ↦ (π_t r')_t` from `Fin (T·B) → Bool` to `Fin T → Fin k → Bool` pushes the uniform
distribution to the uniform one — it is the first projection of a splitting equivalence
`(Fin (T·B) → Bool) ≃ (Fin T → Fin k → Bool) × (Fin T → Fin (B − k) → Bool)` (`uprob_comp_equiv`,
`uprob_fst`; alternatively `pushesUniform_of_card_fiber`) — as does
`Equiv.piCongrRight (fun _ => bitsEquiv k)`; conclude from `statClose_firstHit` (default
`⟨d, hdk⟩`, `hd`) by `StatClose.comp_pushesUniform` and `StatClose.map Fin.val`. -/
theorem statClose_rejectBlocksL (E : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred E] (k B T : ℕ) (hkB : k ≤ B)
    {d : ℕ} (hd : E d) (hdk : d < 2 ^ k) :
    StatClose (fun r : Fin (T * B) → Bool => (rejectBlocksL E k B T (List.ofFn r)).getD d)
      (fun e : {v : Fin (2 ^ k) // E (v : ℕ)} => ((e : Fin (2 ^ k)) : ℕ))
      ((1 - uprob fun v : Fin (2 ^ k) => E (v : ℕ)) ^ T) := by
  -- the numbers read from the blocks, as a uniform draw of `T` elements of `Fin (2^k)`
  let π : (Fin (T * B) → Bool) → Fin T → Fin (2 ^ k) :=
    fun r t => bitsEquiv k (fun j => r (dla_blockPos hkB (t, j)))
  have hπ : HardcoreBit.PushesUniform π := by
    have h1 :=
      HardcoreBit.pushesUniform_restrict (O := Bool) (dla_blockPos_injective (T := T) hkB)
    have h2 := HardcoreBit.pushesUniform_equiv
      ((Equiv.curry (Fin T) (Fin k) Bool).trans (Equiv.piCongrRight fun _ : Fin T => bitsEquiv k))
    exact h1.comp h2
  have h := ((statClose_firstHit (fun v : Fin (2 ^ k) => E (v : ℕ)) T
    (d := ⟨d, hdk⟩) hd).comp_pushesUniform hπ).map Fin.val
  -- the block sampler is the first hit of the numbers read, mapped to `ℕ`
  have hX : ∀ r : Fin (T * B) → Bool, (rejectBlocksL E k B T (List.ofFn r)).getD d =
      ((firstHit (fun v : Fin (2 ^ k) => E (v : ℕ)) (π r)).getD ⟨d, hdk⟩).val := by
    intro r
    have hmap : rejectBlocksL E k B T (List.ofFn r) =
        (firstHit (fun v : Fin (2 ^ k) => E (v : ℕ)) (π r)).map Fin.val := by
      rw [rejectBlocksL_eq, firstHit_eq, List.map_findSome?, ← List.map_coe_finRange,
        List.findSome?_map]
      congr 1
      funext t
      have hv : listToNat (((List.ofFn r).drop (t.val * B)).take k) = (π r t).val := by
        rw [dla_take_drop_ofFn hkB r t, bitsEquiv_val, bitsToNat_eq_listToNat]
      show (if E (listToNat (((List.ofFn r).drop (t.val * B)).take k)) then
          some (listToNat (((List.ofFn r).drop (t.val * B)).take k)) else none) =
        Option.map Fin.val (if E (π r t).val then some (π r t) else none)
      rw [hv]
      by_cases hE : E (π r t).val
      · rw [if_pos hE, if_pos hE, Option.map_some]
      · rw [if_neg hE, if_neg hE, Option.map_none]
    rw [hmap]
    exact Option.getD_map Fin.val ⟨d, hdk⟩ _
  have hX' : (fun r : Fin (T * B) → Bool => (rejectBlocksL E k B T (List.ofFn r)).getD d) =
      fun r => ((firstHit (fun v : Fin (2 ^ k) => E (v : ℕ)) (π r)).getD ⟨d, hdk⟩).val :=
    funext hX
  rw [hX']
  exact h

end TCSlib.Cryptography.Candidates

String) do
    let ns := (catalog[spelling]?).getD #[]
    unless ns.size == 1 do throwError "seal name not found or ambiguous: {spelling}"
    let n := ns[0]!
    let before ← Lean.Elab.Command.liftCoreM <| Lean.getReducibilityStatus n
    if before == .irreducible then
      already := already + 1
    else
      let id := Lean.mkIdent n
      Lean.Elab.Command.elabCommand (← `(command| attribute [local irreducible] $id:ident))
      active := active + 1
    let status ← Lean.Elab.Command.liftCoreM <| Lean.getReducibilityStatus n
    unless status == .irreducible do throwError "seal not installed: {n}"
  Lean.logInfo m!"SUPPLEMENT-SEAL active={active} already={already}"

import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Bits
import Mathlib.Tactic.FinCases
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Primitives
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFindHost
import TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Primitives

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The machine behind the repetition lemma

The finite machine behind `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind`
(`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Repetition`, the load-bearing lemma of the Pass–shelat campaign,
foundation decision D11 of `PassShelatChapter2-4Plan.md`): iterate a polynomial-time step `g`
at most `R(|x|)` times on a polynomially bounded orbit and return the payload `out` of the first
orbit point accepted by `acc` (`[]` on exhaustion). Every theorem of [PS10, ch. 2–4] that
repeats an adversary — Algorithm 38.5's `2nm²p(n)` attempts with first success
[PS10, Theorem 35.1], the `n(2^k − 1)` calls of Goldreich–Levin [PS10, Theorem 87.3], the
truncated simulators [PS10, Algorithms 123.4 and 128.7] — reduces to this machine.

## Construction (DESIGN.md §2.6, the three panel repairs built in)

The machine is an instance of the result-bearing loop combinator
`Turing.FinTM.exists_loopFindTM` (`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Loop`).

1. *State word.* The loop state is the pair `⟨x, s⟩` (`Turing.pairEncode x s`) of the input
   and the current orbit point; the loop invariant `Inv` says the word *is* such a pair with
   `|s| ≤ P|x|`; the step is the length-guarded `Complexity.IterateFind.step`
   (`⟨x, g s⟩` if `|g s| ≤ P|x|`, else unchanged), under which the invariant is closed for
   every admissible word; on the orbit the guard never fires (the pure lemmas of
   `TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Repetition`).
2. *Modules.* Three clean-call modules over the state word, from
   `Turing.FinTM.exists_installCallTM`/`exists_emitCallTM` applied to FP functions: the
   **verdict** install `w ↦ ⟨[acc (snd w)], w⟩` (the verdict as the first cell of the installed
   word), the **step** install `w' ↦ step` on the pair carried by `w'`, and the **payload** emit
   `w' ↦ out (snd (snd w'))`; plus the startup module `x ↦ ⟨x, x⟩`
   (`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairDup`) and a two-state copier that puts the native
   input on tape 0 first.
3. *Gluing.* Each module is converted into a first-halting source (a release flag stops it one
   silent step after its first positive exit), padded to the common tape count, and embedded
   into one finite host through the forwarding transformer `Turing.emitAction`; the host's own
   control has three fresh states — the loop **anchor** (never a module-internal state), a
   **branch** state reading the verdict cell of tape 0, and a **halt** state. Modules return
   to fixed host states: copier → startup install → anchor; verdict → branch; branch → payload
   emit (verdict `true`) or step install (verdict `false`); payload emit → halt; step → anchor.
4. *Budgets.* All requests are state words of length at most `Q n + 4` with
   `Q n = 2n + 2 + P n`; every module's polynomial budget on its argument is majorised by one
   common `A · (Q n + 5)^D`, which also pays for the fuel machine `x ↦ Nat.bits (R|x|)`
   (`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly R` composed with
   `Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_lengthBits`, so that the `find?` range is exactly
   `R|x| + 1`). The loop combinator returns a machine within `c (T n + 1)(R n + 2)`, which
   `PolyExpr.eval_le` puts in the normal form of `Complexity.PolyTimeComputable`.

The clean modules and the finite host (steps 2–3: release-flag stop, padding, forwarding host,
first-halt cutting) are the public clean-module host
`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.ModuleHost` (host H14 of `machine-library-design.md` §14);
its instance for this machine (the copier, the control table, the return states) lives in
`TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.Build.IterateFindHost`.
This file supplies the pure step, the FP functions of the modules, the budget arithmetic, and the
assembly through `Turing.FinTM.exists_loopFindTM`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.IterateFind.step` — the length-guarded step on the state word (definitionally
  `Complexity.guardedStep`).

## Main results

* `Complexity.IterateFind.polyTimeComputable_find` — the loop-level form of the repetition
  lemma: the first accepted orbit point's payload along the guarded orbit of `⟨x, x⟩` is
  polynomial-time computable.
* `Complexity.IterateFind.find?_congr_of_mem` — `List.find?` depends only on the predicate's
  values on the list (used to identify the guarded orbit with `g^[i] x`).
* `Complexity.IterateFind.find?_range_and_lt` — a search over `[0, L)` whose test also demands
  `i < N` is the search over `[0, N)`, for `N ≤ L`.

## References

* [PS10] R. Pass, a. shelat, *A Course in Cryptography*, lecture notes, 3rd ed., January 2010.
  (Algorithm 38.5 and Theorem 35.1; Theorem 87.3; Algorithms 123.4 and 128.7.)
* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.2–1.3, time-bounded machines.)
-/

namespace Complexity.IterateFind

open Turing

/-! ### The guarded step on the state word and its FP pieces -/

/-- The length-guarded step on the state word `w = ⟨x, s⟩`: advance to `⟨x, g s⟩` if the new
orbit point fits the bound `P|x|`, else stay (DESIGN.md §2.6, step 1). This is definitionally
`Complexity.guardedStep g P x w`; it is restated here because this file is imported by the
file defining `guardedStep`. -/
def step (g : List Bool → List Bool) (P : PolyExpr) (x w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if (g (pairSndD w)).length ≤ P.eval x.length then pairEncode x (g (pairSndD w)) else w

/-- The guarded step: `step g P x w = ⟨x, g (snd w)⟩` if `|g (snd w)| ≤ P|x|`, and `w`
otherwise. -/
theorem step_eq (g : List Bool → List Bool) (P : PolyExpr) (x w : List Bool) :
    step g P x w =
      if (g (pairSndD w)).length ≤ P.eval x.length then pairEncode x (g (pairSndD w)) else w :=
  rfl

/-- The loop invariant used by the machine: the state word *is* a pair `⟨x, s⟩` with
`|s| ≤ P|x|` (stronger than the pure `Complexity.LoopInv`, which also admits malformed
words; the machine needs the well-formedness to bound the word's length). -/
private def Inv (P : PolyExpr) (x w : List Bool) : Prop :=
  ∃ s, w = pairEncode x s ∧ s.length ≤ P.eval x.length

/-- The initial word `⟨x, x⟩` is admissible when `|x| ≤ P|x|`. -/
private theorem inv_init (P : PolyExpr) (x : List Bool) (h0 : x.length ≤ P.eval x.length) :
    Inv P x (pairEncode x x) :=
  ⟨x, rfl, h0⟩

/-- The invariant is closed under the guarded step (the guard keeps the word unchanged when
the new point would be too long). -/
private theorem inv_step (g : List Bool → List Bool) (P : PolyExpr) (x w : List Bool)
    (h : Inv P x w) : Inv P x (step g P x w) := by
  obtain ⟨s, rfl, hs⟩ := h
  unfold step
  rw [pairSndD_pairEncode]
  split_ifs with hg
  · exact ⟨g s, rfl, hg⟩
  · exact ⟨s, rfl, hs⟩

/-- The length of an admissible state word is at most `2|x| + 2 + P|x|`. -/
private theorem inv_length (P : PolyExpr) (x w : List Bool) (h : Inv P x w) :
    w.length ≤ 2 * x.length + 2 + P.eval x.length := by
  obtain ⟨s, rfl, hs⟩ := h
  rw [length_pairEncode]
  omega

/-- The verdict word: `w ↦ ⟨[acc (snd w)], w⟩` (the verdict as the first cell, since
`pairEncode [b] w = [b, b, false, true] ++ w`). -/
private def verdictWord (acc : List Bool → Bool) (w : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode [acc (pairSndD w)] w

/-- The step on a verdict word: strip the verdict, then take the guarded step on the pair
`⟨x, s⟩` carried by the word, with `x` recovered from the word itself. -/
private def stepWord (g : List Bool → List Bool) (P : PolyExpr) (w' : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  if (g (pairSndD (pairSndD w'))).length ≤ P.eval (pairFstD (pairSndD w')).length then
    pairEncode (pairFstD (pairSndD w')) (g (pairSndD (pairSndD w')))
  else pairSndD w'

/-- The payload of a verdict word: `out` of the orbit point `snd (snd w')`. -/
private def outWord (out : List Bool → List Bool) (w' : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  out (pairSndD (pairSndD w'))

/-- The first cell of a verdict word is the verdict. -/
private theorem verdictWord_head (acc : List Bool → Bool) (w : List Bool) :
    (verdictWord acc w)[0]? = some (acc (pairSndD w)) := by
  simp [verdictWord, pairEncode]

/-- The length of a verdict word. -/
private theorem verdictWord_length (acc : List Bool → Bool) (w : List Bool) :
    (verdictWord acc w).length = w.length + 4 := by
  simp [verdictWord, length_pairEncode]
  omega

/-- On the verdict word of a pair `⟨x, s⟩`, `stepWord` is the guarded step. -/
private theorem stepWord_verdictWord (g : List Bool → List Bool) (P : PolyExpr)
    (acc : List Bool → Bool) (x s : List Bool) :
    stepWord g P (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)) = step g P x (pairEncode x s) := by
  simp [stepWord, verdictWord, step]

/-- On the verdict word of a pair, `outWord` is `out` of the orbit point. -/
private theorem outWord_verdictWord (out : List Bool → List Bool) (acc : List Bool → Bool)
    (x s : List Bool) : outWord out (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)) = out s := by
  simp [outWord, verdictWord]

/-- The verdict word is polynomial-time computable (`PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode` of the
test composed with the projection and the identity). -/
private theorem verdictWord_poly {acc : List Bool → Bool}
    (hacc : PolyTimeComputable fun s => [acc s]) : PolyTimeComputable (verdictWord acc) := by
  have h := (hacc.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD).pairEncode polyTimeComputable_id
  exact h

/-- The step on verdict words is polynomial-time computable.

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_ite`: the test
`|g (snd (snd w'))| ≤ P|fst (snd w')|` is `Complexity.polyTimeComputable_lenLe` on the pair
`⟨1^{P|fst (snd w')|}, g (snd (snd w'))⟩`, built with the unary evaluator
`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly P` and `PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode`; the `then`
branch is the pairing of the two projections (with `g`), the `else` branch the projection
`snd`; the Boolean test is identified with the propositional `if` by `decide_eq_true_eq`. -/
private theorem stepWord_poly {g : List Bool → List Bool} (hg : PolyTimeComputable g)
    (P : PolyExpr) : PolyTimeComputable (stepWord g P) := by
  have hs2 : PolyTimeComputable fun w' => pairSndD (pairSndD w') :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  have hf1 : PolyTimeComputable fun w' => pairFstD (pairSndD w') :=
    polyTimeComputable_pairFstD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  have hgg : PolyTimeComputable fun w' => g (pairSndD (pairSndD w')) := hg.comp hs2
  have hun : PolyTimeComputable fun w' =>
      List.replicate (P.eval (pairFstD (pairSndD w')).length) true :=
    (polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly P).comp hf1
  have htest : PolyTimeComputable fun w' =>
      [decide ((g (pairSndD (pairSndD w'))).length ≤ P.eval (pairFstD (pairSndD w')).length)] := by
    have h := polyTimeComputable_lenLe.comp (hun.pairEncode hgg)
    convert h using 1
    funext w'
    simp
  have hthen : PolyTimeComputable fun w' =>
      pairEncode (pairFstD (pairSndD w')) (g (pairSndD (pairSndD w'))) := hf1.pairEncode hgg
  have h := polyTimeComputable_ite htest hthen polyTimeComputable_pairSndD
  convert h using 1
  funext w'
  simp [stepWord]

/-- The payload map on verdict words is polynomial-time computable. -/
private theorem outWord_poly {out : List Bool → List Bool} (hout : PolyTimeComputable out) :
    PolyTimeComputable (outWord out) :=
  hout.comp (polyTimeComputable_pairSndD.comp polyTimeComputable_pairSndD)

/-- The duplication `x ↦ ⟨x, x⟩` is polynomial-time computable. -/
private theorem dupWord_poly : PolyTimeComputable fun x => pairEncode x x :=
  polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairDup

/-! ### Assembly -/

/-- `List.find?` depends only on the values of the predicate on the list's elements. -/
theorem find?_congr_of_mem {α : Type*} {p q : α → Bool} :
    ∀ l : List α, (∀ a ∈ l, p a = q a) → l.find? p = l.find? q
  | [], _ => rfl
  | a :: l, h => by
    have ha : p a = q a := h a (List.mem_cons_self ..)
    by_cases hq : q a = true
    · rw [List.find?_cons_of_pos (by rw [ha]; exact hq), List.find?_cons_of_pos hq]
    · rw [List.find?_cons_of_neg (by rw [ha]; exact hq), List.find?_cons_of_neg hq]
      exact find?_congr_of_mem l (fun b hb => h b (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hb))

/-- **A bounded search is a search over a shorter range**: for `N ≤ L`, searching `[0, L)` for
the first `i` with `i < N` and `p i` is searching `[0, N)` for the first `i` with `p i`:
`(List.range L).find? (fun i => decide (i < N) && p i) = (List.range N).find? p`.

**Proof sketch.** Write `L = N + d` (`List.range_add`, `List.find?_append`). On `[0, N)` the guard
`i < N` holds, so the two predicates agree (`find?_congr_of_mem`). On the shifted tail `N + [0, d)`
it fails, so that search is `none` (`List.find?_eq_none`), and `o <|> none = o`. -/
theorem find?_range_and_lt (p : ℕ → Bool) {N L : ℕ} (hNL : N ≤ L) :
    (List.range L).find? (fun i => decide (i < N) && p i) = (List.range N).find? p := by
  obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hNL
  rw [List.range_add, List.find?_append,
    find?_congr_of_mem _ (fun i hi => by rw [decide_eq_true (List.mem_range.1 hi), Bool.true_and])]
  have hnone : (List.map (fun x => N + x) (List.range d)).find?
      (fun i => decide (i < N) && p i) = none := by
    rw [List.find?_eq_none]
    intro x hx
    obtain ⟨y, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hx
    rw [decide_eq_false (by omega), Bool.false_and]
    exact Bool.false_ne_true
  rw [hnone, Option.or_none]

/-- The final budget arithmetic: the loop combinator's bound `c (T n + 1)(R n + 2)` with
`T n = A (2n + 2 + P n + 5)^D` is in the normal form `C (n + 1)^e` once `P` and `R` are
majorised by `CP (n+1)^cP` and `CR (n+1)^cR`.

**Proof sketch.** `2n + 7 + P n ≤ (CP + 7)(n+1)^{cP+1}` (both `7(n+1)` and `CP (n+1)^{cP}`
are at most the corresponding multiples of `(n+1)^{cP+1}`); raise to the `D`-th power
(`Nat.pow_le_pow_left`, `Nat.mul_pow`, `Nat.pow_mul`), absorb the `+ 1` with
`1 ≤ (n+1)^{(cP+1)D}`, bound `R n + 2 ≤ (CR + 2)(n+1)^{cR}` likewise, and multiply
(`Nat.mul_le_mul`, `Nat.pow_add`). -/
private lemma final_bound (c A D CP cP CR cR n Pn Rn : ℕ)
    (hP : Pn ≤ CP * (n + 1) ^ cP) (hR : Rn ≤ CR * (n + 1) ^ cR) :
    c * (A * (2 * n + 2 + Pn + 5) ^ D + 1) * (Rn + 2) ≤
      c * (A * (CP + 7) ^ D + 1) * (CR + 2) * (n + 1) ^ ((cP + 1) * D + cR) := by
  have hpos : 0 < n + 1 := Nat.succ_pos n
  have h1 : 2 * n + 2 + Pn + 5 ≤ (CP + 7) * (n + 1) ^ (cP + 1) := by
    have ha : n + 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ (cP + 1) := by
      simpa using Nat.pow_le_pow_right hpos (show 1 ≤ cP + 1 by omega)
    have hb : (n + 1) ^ cP ≤ (n + 1) ^ (cP + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hpos (by omega)
    have hc := Nat.mul_le_mul_left CP hb
    calc 2 * n + 2 + Pn + 5 ≤ 7 * (n + 1) + CP * (n + 1) ^ cP := by omega
      _ ≤ 7 * (n + 1) ^ (cP + 1) + CP * (n + 1) ^ (cP + 1) :=
          Nat.add_le_add (Nat.mul_le_mul_left 7 ha) hc
      _ = (CP + 7) * (n + 1) ^ (cP + 1) := by ring
  have h2 : (2 * n + 2 + Pn + 5) ^ D ≤ (CP + 7) ^ D * (n + 1) ^ ((cP + 1) * D) := by
    calc (2 * n + 2 + Pn + 5) ^ D ≤ ((CP + 7) * (n + 1) ^ (cP + 1)) ^ D :=
          Nat.pow_le_pow_left h1 D
      _ = (CP + 7) ^ D * (n + 1) ^ ((cP + 1) * D) := by rw [Nat.mul_pow, ← Nat.pow_mul]
  have hone : 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ ((cP + 1) * D) := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ hpos
  have h3 : A * (2 * n + 2 + Pn + 5) ^ D + 1 ≤
      (A * (CP + 7) ^ D + 1) * (n + 1) ^ ((cP + 1) * D) := by
    calc A * (2 * n + 2 + Pn + 5) ^ D + 1
        ≤ A * ((CP + 7) ^ D * (n + 1) ^ ((cP + 1) * D)) + (n + 1) ^ ((cP + 1) * D) :=
          Nat.add_le_add (Nat.mul_le_mul_left A h2) hone
      _ = (A * (CP + 7) ^ D + 1) * (n + 1) ^ ((cP + 1) * D) := by ring
  have h4 : Rn + 2 ≤ (CR + 2) * (n + 1) ^ cR := by
    have hone' : 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ cR := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ hpos
    calc Rn + 2 ≤ CR * (n + 1) ^ cR + 2 * (n + 1) ^ cR := by omega
      _ = (CR + 2) * (n + 1) ^ cR := by ring
  calc c * (A * (2 * n + 2 + Pn + 5) ^ D + 1) * (Rn + 2)
      ≤ c * ((A * (CP + 7) ^ D + 1) * (n + 1) ^ ((cP + 1) * D)) * ((CR + 2) * (n + 1) ^ cR) :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul_left c h3) h4
    _ = c * (A * (CP + 7) ^ D + 1) * (CR + 2) * (n + 1) ^ ((cP + 1) * D + cR) := by
        rw [Nat.pow_add]; ring

/-- **The loop-level repetition lemma.** Let `g` be a polynomial-time step, `acc` a
polynomial-time test, `out` a polynomial-time payload map, and `R, P` syntactic polynomials
with `|g^[i] x| ≤ P|x|` for `i ≤ R|x|`. Then the function returning `out` of the orbit point
of the first index `i ≤ R|x|` at which `acc` accepts the second component of the `i`-fold
guarded step `Complexity.IterateFind.step g P x` from `⟨x, x⟩` (`[]` if none) is
polynomial-time computable. This is the machine behind
`Complexity.polyTimeComputable_iterateFind` [PS10, Algorithm 38.5, Theorem 35.1]; the pure
identification of the guarded orbit with `g^[i] x` is done there.

**Proof sketch.** Instance of `Turing.FinTM.exists_loopFindTM` for the host `hostTM` (the
clean-module host `Turing.ModuleHost.hostTM` with the control table `hostCtrl`) over the five
clean modules (the copier, and `Turing.ModuleHost.clean_install`/`clean_emit` of
`x ↦ ⟨x, x⟩`, `verdictWord acc`, `stepWord g P`, `outWord out`), with anchor `inl 0`,
invariant `Inv P`,
step `step g P`, acceptance `acc ∘ snd`, payload `out ∘ snd`, start word `⟨x, x⟩`. The fuel
machine computes `Nat.bits (R|x|)` (`polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly R` composed with
`computesFunInTime_lengthBits`). `hstart`: the copier (`copy_clean`, `ModuleHost.host_call`)
then the startup install (`ModuleHost.host_clean`) reach the anchor seam with `⟨x, x⟩` in
`2|x| + 2 + t_S` steps
with no earlier anchor visit. `hround`: from the anchor seam with an admissible word `⟨x, s⟩`,
the dispatch step, the verdict call, the branch step (`host_branch`), then either the payload
call and the halt step (`host_halt`) — state `none`, output `out s` — or the step call
returning to the anchor seam with `step g P x ⟨x, s⟩` (`stepWord_verdictWord`); the anchor
guard is `ModuleHost.guard_add` over the segments. All requests have length at most
`2|x| + 2 + P|x| + 4`, so every call fits the common budget `T n = A (2n + 2 + P n + 5)^D`
(`ModuleHost.request_budget`), and
`final_bound` puts the combinator's bound `c (T n + 1)(R n + 2)` in normal form. -/
theorem polyTimeComputable_find {g : List Bool → List Bool} (hg : PolyTimeComputable g)
    {acc : List Bool → Bool} (hacc : PolyTimeComputable fun s => [acc s])
    {out : List Bool → List Bool} (hout : PolyTimeComputable out)
    (R P : PolyExpr)
    (horbit : ∀ (x : List Bool) (i : ℕ), i ≤ R.eval x.length →
      (g^[i] x).length ≤ P.eval x.length) :
    PolyTimeComputable fun x =>
      match (List.range (R.eval x.length + 1)).find?
          (fun i => acc (pairSndD ((step g P x)^[i] (pairEncode x x)))) with
      | some i => out (pairSndD ((step g P x)^[i] (pairEncode x x)))
      | none => [] := by
  obtain ⟨S, aS, dS, hS⟩ := ModuleHost.clean_install dupWord_poly
  obtain ⟨V, aV, dV, hV⟩ := ModuleHost.clean_install (verdictWord_poly hacc)
  obtain ⟨I, aI, dI, hI⟩ := ModuleHost.clean_install (stepWord_poly hg P)
  obtain ⟨E, aE, dE, hE⟩ := ModuleHost.clean_emit (outWord_poly hout)
  obtain ⟨F, aF, dF, hF⟩ : PolyTimeComputable fun x => Nat.bits (R.eval x.length) := by
    have h := (polyTimeComputable_of_linear FinTM.computesFunInTime_lengthBits).comp
      (polyTimeComputable_unaryPoly R)
    convert h using 1
    funext x
    simp
  let M : Fin 5 → FinTM Bool := fun i => match i.val with
    | 0 => copyTM | 1 => S | 2 => V | 3 => I | _ => E
  let K := S.k + V.k + I.k + E.k
  have hk : ∀ i, (M i).k ≤ K + 1 := by
    intro i; fin_cases i <;> simp [M, K, copyTM_k] <;> omega
  let H := hostTM M K hk
  let anchor : H.State := .inl 0
  have hclean := ModuleHost.host_clean M (K + 1) hk (hostCtrl M K) (hostRet M)
    (ModuleHost.entry M 0)
  let D := dS + dV + dI + dE + dF + 1
  let A := aS + aV + aI + aE + aF + 5
  let pow (n : ℕ) := (2 * n + 2 + P.eval n + 5) ^ D
  let T (n : ℕ) := A * pow n
  have hpow (n : ℕ) : n + 1 ≤ pow n := by
    have h := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (show 0 < 2 * n + 2 + P.eval n + 5 by omega)
      (show 1 ≤ D by dsimp [D]; omega)
    simp only [Nat.pow_one] at h
    exact (by omega : n + 1 ≤ 2 * n + 2 + P.eval n + 5).trans h
  have hstart : ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ t ≤ T x.length,
      (∀ v < t, (H.tm.runFrom (H.tm.initCfg x) v).state ≠ some anchor) ∧
      H.tm.runFrom (H.tm.initCfg x) t = Cfg.ofWords anchor (stateWord H.k (pairEncode x x)) := by
    intro x
    obtain ⟨hcg, hce⟩ := copy_clean x
    obtain ⟨hcGuard, hcEnd⟩ := ModuleHost.host_call M (K + 1) hk (hostCtrl M K) (hostRet M)
      (ModuleHost.entry M 0) 0 (by simp [M, copyTM_k]) x [] x [] [] (0 : Fin 2)
      (2 * x.length + 2) hcg (by simpa using hce)
    have hi : H.tm.initCfg x = Cfg.ofWords (ModuleHost.entry M 0) (stateWord (K + 1) []) := by
      refine Cfg.ext ?_ rfl ?_ rfl rfl
      · exact congrArg some (ModuleHost.hostTM_tm_q₀ M (K + 1) hk (hostCtrl M K) (hostRet M)
          (ModuleHost.entry M 0))
      funext i z
      simp [MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init, Cfg.ofWords, stateWord]
    change H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (ModuleHost.entry M 0) (stateWord (K + 1) []))
      (2 * x.length + 2) = Cfg.ofWords (hostRet M 0) (stateWord (K + 1) x) at hcEnd
    rw [hostRet_zero] at hcEnd
    obtain ⟨ts, hspos, hst, hsGuard, hsEnd⟩ := hclean 1
      (fun x => pairEncode x x) (fun _ => []) (fun n => aS * (n + 1) ^ dS)
      (by simpa [M] using hS) x x []
    change H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (ModuleHost.entry M 1) (stateWord (K + 1) x))
      ts = Cfg.ofWords (hostRet M 1) (stateWord (K + 1) (pairEncode x x)) at hsEnd
    rw [hostRet_one] at hsEnd
    have hsB := ModuleHost.request_budget aS dS D (2 * x.length + 2 + P.eval x.length + 5) x.length
      (by dsimp [D]; omega) (by omega)
    have hp := hpow x.length
    refine ⟨2 * x.length + 2 + ts, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · dsimp only [T, A, pow]
      simp only [Nat.add_mul]
      dsimp only [pow] at hp
      omega
    · rw [hi]
      exact ModuleHost.guard_add H.tm anchor _ _ _ ts (fun v hv => hcGuard v hv 0) hcEnd
        (fun v hv => hsGuard v hv 0)
    · rw [hi, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, hcEnd, hsEnd]
      rfl
  have hround : ∀ x w : List Bool, Inv P x w → ∃ t, 0 < t ∧ t ≤ T x.length ∧
      (∀ t', 0 < t' → t' < t →
        (H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) anchor (stateWord H.k w)) t').state
          ≠ some anchor) ∧
      if acc (pairSndD w) then
        (H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) anchor (stateWord H.k w)) t).state = none ∧
        (H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) anchor (stateWord H.k w)) t).output =
          out (pairSndD w)
      else
        H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) anchor (stateWord H.k w)) t =
          Cfg.ofWords anchor (stateWord H.k (step g P x w)) := by
    intro x w hw
    obtain ⟨s, rfl, hs⟩ := hw
    have hwlen : (pairEncode x s).length ≤ 2 * x.length + 2 + P.eval x.length := by
      rw [length_pairEncode]; omega
    have hw'len : (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)).length =
        (pairEncode x s).length + 4 := verdictWord_length acc _
    have hpow' := hpow x.length
    -- the dispatch, the verdict call, the branch
    have hdisp := host_dispatch M K hk x (pairEncode x s)
    obtain ⟨tv, hvpos, hvt, hvGuard, hvEnd⟩ := hclean 2 (verdictWord acc)
      (fun _ => []) (fun n => aV * (n + 1) ^ dV) (by simpa [M] using hV) x (pairEncode x s) []
    change H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (ModuleHost.entry M 2) (stateWord (K + 1)
      (pairEncode x s))) tv = Cfg.ofWords (hostRet M 2) (stateWord (K + 1)
        (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s))) at hvEnd
    rw [hostRet_two] at hvEnd
    have hbr := host_branch M K hk x (acc s) (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s))
      (by rw [verdictWord_head, pairSndD_pairEncode])
    have hvB := ModuleHost.request_budget aV dV D (2 * x.length + 2 + P.eval x.length + 5)
      (pairEncode x s).length (by dsimp [D]; omega) (by omega)
    have hseg : H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (ModuleHost.entry M 2)
        (stateWord (K + 1) (pairEncode x s))) (tv + 1) =
        Cfg.ofWords (ModuleHost.entry M (if acc s then 4 else 3))
          (stateWord (K + 1) (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s))) := by
      rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', hvEnd, hbr]
    have hsegGuard : ∀ v < tv + 1, (H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (ModuleHost.entry M 2)
        (stateWord (K + 1) (pairEncode x s))) v).state ≠ some anchor := by
      refine ModuleHost.guard_add H.tm anchor _ _ tv 1 (fun v hv => hvGuard v hv 0) hvEnd ?_
      intro v hv
      have hv0 : v = 0 := by omega
      subst hv0
      simp [Cfg.ofWords, anchor]
    by_cases hb : acc s = true
    · -- accepting round: the payload call, then the halt
      rw [if_pos hb] at hseg
      obtain ⟨te, hepos, het, heGuard, heEnd⟩ := hclean 4 id (outWord out)
        (fun n => aE * (n + 1) ^ dE) (by simpa [M] using hE) x
        (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)) []
      change H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (ModuleHost.entry M 4) (stateWord (K + 1)
        (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)))) te = {Cfg.ofWords (hostRet M 4) (stateWord (K + 1)
          (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s))) with
            output := [] ++ outWord out (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s))} at heEnd
      rw [hostRet_four, List.nil_append, outWord_verdictWord] at heEnd
      have hhalt := host_halt M K hk x (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)) (out s)
      have heB := ModuleHost.request_budget aE dE D (2 * x.length + 2 + P.eval x.length + 5)
        (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)).length (by dsimp [D]; omega) (by omega)
      have hall : H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (ModuleHost.entry M 2)
          (stateWord (K + 1) (pairEncode x s))) (tv + 1 + te + 1) =
          {Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (.inl 2 : ModuleHost.State (Fin 3) M) (stateWord (K + 1)
            (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s))) with state := none, output := out s} := by
        rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, hseg, heEnd, hhalt]
      have hallGuard : ∀ v < tv + 1 + te + 1, (H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x)
          (ModuleHost.entry M 2) (stateWord (K + 1) (pairEncode x s))) v).state ≠ some anchor := by
        refine ModuleHost.guard_add H.tm anchor _ {Cfg.ofWords (input := x)
          (.inl 2 : ModuleHost.State (Fin 3) M)
          (stateWord (K + 1) (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s))) with output := out s}
          (tv + 1 + te) 1 ?_ ?_ ?_
        · exact ModuleHost.guard_add H.tm anchor _ _ (tv + 1) te hsegGuard hseg
            (fun v hv => heGuard v hv 0)
        · rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, hseg, heEnd]
        · intro v hv
          have hv0 : v = 0 := by omega
          subst hv0
          simp [Cfg.ofWords, anchor]
      refine ⟨tv + 1 + te + 1 + 1, by omega, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · dsimp only [T, A, pow]
        simp only [Nat.add_mul]
        dsimp only [pow] at hpow'
        omega
      · intro v hv hvt
        have hvform : v = (v - 1) + 1 := by omega
        change (H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) anchor (stateWord (K + 1)
          (pairEncode x s))) v).state ≠ some anchor
        rw [hvform, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, hdisp]
        exact hallGuard (v - 1) (by omega)
      · rw [pairSndD_pairEncode, if_pos hb]
        change (H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) anchor (stateWord (K + 1)
            (pairEncode x s))) (tv + 1 + te + 1 + 1)).state = none ∧
          (H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) anchor (stateWord (K + 1)
            (pairEncode x s))) (tv + 1 + te + 1 + 1)).output = out s
        rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, hdisp, hall]
        exact ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    · -- advancing round: the step call returns to the anchor
      rw [if_neg hb] at hseg
      obtain ⟨ti, hipos, hit, hiGuard, hiEnd⟩ := hclean 3 (stepWord g P)
        (fun _ => []) (fun n => aI * (n + 1) ^ dI) (by simpa [M] using hI) x
        (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)) []
      change H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (ModuleHost.entry M 3) (stateWord (K + 1)
        (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)))) ti = Cfg.ofWords (hostRet M 3) (stateWord (K + 1)
          (stepWord g P (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)))) at hiEnd
      rw [hostRet_three, stepWord_verdictWord] at hiEnd
      have hiB := ModuleHost.request_budget aI dI D (2 * x.length + 2 + P.eval x.length + 5)
        (verdictWord acc (pairEncode x s)).length (by dsimp [D]; omega) (by omega)
      have hall : H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) (ModuleHost.entry M 2)
          (stateWord (K + 1) (pairEncode x s))) (tv + 1 + ti) =
          Cfg.ofWords anchor (stateWord (K + 1) (step g P x (pairEncode x s))) := by
        rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, hseg, hiEnd]
      have hallGuard : ∀ v < tv + 1 + ti, (H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x)
          (ModuleHost.entry M 2) (stateWord (K + 1) (pairEncode x s))) v).state ≠ some anchor :=
        ModuleHost.guard_add H.tm anchor _ _ (tv + 1) ti hsegGuard hseg
          (fun v hv => hiGuard v hv 0)
      refine ⟨tv + 1 + ti + 1, by omega, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · dsimp only [T, A, pow]
        simp only [Nat.add_mul]
        dsimp only [pow] at hpow'
        omega
      · intro v hv hvt
        have hvform : v = (v - 1) + 1 := by omega
        change (H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) anchor (stateWord (K + 1)
          (pairEncode x s))) v).state ≠ some anchor
        rw [hvform, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, hdisp]
        exact hallGuard (v - 1) (by omega)
      · rw [pairSndD_pairEncode, if_neg hb]
        change H.tm.runFrom (Cfg.ofWords (input := x) anchor (stateWord (K + 1)
            (pairEncode x s))) (tv + 1 + ti + 1) =
          Cfg.ofWords anchor (stateWord (K + 1) (step g P x (pairEncode x s)))
        rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, hdisp, hall]
  have hFuel : F.ComputesFunInTime (fun x => Nat.bits (R.eval x.length)) T := by
    intro x
    apply (hF x).mono
    have h := ModuleHost.request_budget aF dF D (2 * x.length + 2 + P.eval x.length + 5) x.length
      (by dsimp [D]; omega) (by omega)
    have hp := hpow x.length
    dsimp only [T, A, pow]
    simp only [Nat.add_mul]
    dsimp only [pow] at hp
    omega
  obtain ⟨L, c, hL⟩ := FinTM.exists_loopFindTM H F anchor (Inv P) (step g P)
    (fun _ w => acc (pairSndD w)) (fun _ w => out (pairSndD w)) (fun x => pairEncode x x)
    (fun n => R.eval n) T hFuel
    (fun x => inv_init P x (by simpa using horbit x 0 (Nat.zero_le _)))
    (fun x w h => inv_step g P x w h) hstart hround
  obtain ⟨CP, cP, hCP⟩ := P.eval_le
  obtain ⟨CR, cR, hCR⟩ := R.eval_le
  refine ⟨L, c * (A * (CP + 7) ^ D + 1) * (CR + 2), (cP + 1) * D + cR, fun x => (hL x).mono ?_⟩
  exact final_bound c A D CP cP CR cR x.length (P.eval x.length) (R.eval x.length)
    (hCP _) (hCR _)

end Complexity.IterateFind

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/Randomized/Closure.lean =====

/-
